fix: In ParseWholeDouble, reject non-finite results (return false unless std::isfinite(out)); in CompareNumericValues decide with `if (da < db) return -1; if (db < da) return 1; return 0;` instead of `da != db`.
problem: CompareNumericValues' double path accepts NaN: strtod parses "nan"/"NaN" (and "inf") as a whole-string match, so for a "number"-typed column with two NaN cells `da != db` is true and `(da < db)` is false, returning +1 for BOTH Compare(a,b) and Compare(b,a). That comparator is fed straight into std::stable_sort in Source/Core/src/Ui/SmatchetActiveProjectGridTable.cpp:205, violating strict weak ordering (UB / nondeterministic grid order).

Callers then treat them as dates: TicketGridModel.cpp:204 sets IsDateLike, and SmatchetGridUiSupport.cpp:359 routes copy through DisplayValueForTrackerDateField for a raw seconds value.

fix: Reject up front when the string is empty or `std::isspace((unsigned char)s[0])`, and for the double path reject a leading "0x"/"0X" prefix (or use a stricter parse), so the comment's contract holds.

Sorting silently disagrees with the displayed text.

fix: Split the two cases: only `continue` when the agent legitimately has no claude-code hint block at all; when either key is present-but-partial, or when both are absent on a non-README agent, record a mismatch (e.g. `model_mismatch+=("$base: no model: key — agent will inherit the session model")`) instead of skipping.
problem: Check 15 fails OPEN on the case it exists to catch: `[[ -z "$hint_model" ]] && continue` skips any agent whose harness-hints claude-code model is missing, and the check never asserts that a top-level `model:` exists at all. Check 5 skips on the same condition (line 186), so an agent file with NO model keys passes every gate and silently inherits the opus-class session model — the exact regression this PR was written to prevent. The check's own header comment (lines 427-431) says "Both must exist and agree".

fix: Anchor the extraction to the claude-code block, e.g. `awk '/^ claude-code:/{c=1;next} c&&/^ [^ ]/{c=0} c' "$f" | grep -m1 -E '^ model:'` (same fix applies to the check-5 copy at lines 184-185).
problem: `awk '/^harness-hints:/,/^---/' | grep -E "^ model:" | head -1` is not scoped to the `claude-code:` sub-block — it takes the first 4-space-indented `model:` under harness-hints regardless of harness. `.coderabbit.yaml` (lines 156-158, also touched by this PR) explicitly documents `harness-hints.<harness>:` blocks such as `harness-hints.claude:` as intentional, so the moment any agent lists a second harness before `claude-code:`, check 15 compares the top-level `model:` against the wrong harness and emits a false PASS or a false FAIL. The awk range also runs to EOF if the frontmatter terminator is missing.

fix: Seed the default before doubling: `MERGE_GATES_MAX_POLLS=$(( ${MERGE_GATES_MAX_POLLS:-90} * 2 ))`.
problem: The verbatim "Keep waiting" branch does `MERGE_GATES_MAX_POLLS=$((MERGE_GATES_MAX_POLLS*2))`. The variable is normally UNSET (merge-gates.sh:345 supplies the default 90), so the arithmetic evaluates to 0 and exports `MERGE_GATES_MAX_POLLS=0` — set-and-non-empty, so `${MERGE_GATES_MAX_POLLS:-90}` no longer defaults, and `TIMEOUT_SECONDS` derives to 0 (merge-gates.sh:350). The re-poll returns immediately non-zero and `|| exit 1` abandons the merge. The user-facing option "Keep waiting (double MAX_POLLS)" therefore aborts instead of waiting.

fix: Use `n * (n - 1) // 2` in the complexity string (and fix the bats comment), or count ordered comparisons consistently on both sides.
problem: The emitted `complexity` string compares the pivot-tournament budget (unordered: n + k(n-k) + C(k,2)) against `n*(n-1)`, the ORDERED all-pairs count. Round-robin is C(n,2)=n(n-1)/2, so the printed savings are inflated 2x and are false for small N: at N=4,k=2 the schedule needs 9 comparisons vs 6 real round-robin pairs, yet the string claims '9 vs 12'. tests/bats/verifier_sidecar.bats:98 enshrines the same wrong baseline in its comment.

fix: Catch `OSError` and `UnicodeDecodeError` in load_json and re-raise as VerifierError so every bad-input path exits 2.
problem: load_json catches only FileNotFoundError and JSONDecodeError, and main() catches only AssertionError/VerifierError, so a directory path, an unreadable file, or a non-UTF-8 file escapes as a raw traceback with exit 1 — violating the documented exit-code contract (0 success / 2 malformed input or usage). Verified: `verifier-sidecar.py aggregate docs` prints an IsADirectoryError traceback.

fix: Anchor the letter parse: only accept the response when the stripped text is a single A-T letter (or the first token after stripping punctuation is one char in _LETTER_SET); otherwise fall through to the numeric parse and raise ProduceError if that fails too.
problem: extract_scalar scans EVERY character of the response text and returns on the first one that happens to fall in A-T, with no anchoring. Any preamble silently yields a wrong score instead of an error: "Score: B" returns 'S' -> 0.053 (near-worst) rather than B -> 0.947; "The answer" returns 'T' -> 0.0. Scalar mode is exactly the path used for backends prone to a short preamble, so candidates get silently mis-ranked with no failure signal.

fix: Accumulate in probability space: out[letter] = log(exp(out[letter]) + exp(lp)) (or math.logaddexp) instead of max().
problem: When two top_logprobs entries normalize to the same letter (e.g. tokens "A" and " A"), the code keeps max(logprob) instead of summing the probability mass. The letter's true mass is p1+p2, so the distribution the whole sidecar consumes (expectation, variance, uncertainty) is systematically understated for any backend that tokenizes the letter with a leading space.

fix: Either invert the 1-20 branch to match the letter rank convention ((GRANULARITY - num) / (GRANULARITY - 1)) or document explicitly in the docstring that bare numbers are higher-is-better while letters are ranks.
problem: Polarity mismatch between the two scalar scales. The letter scale is a rank where A (position 1) = 1.0 = best, but the bare-number 1-20 branch maps 1 -> 0.0 and 20 -> 1.0, i.e. higher-is-better. A model that answers "1" meaning rank 1 (best) is scored as worst.

problem: HttpTransport accepts plain http:// endpoints and then unconditionally attaches the Authorization: Bearer VERIFIER_API_KEY header, so the key travels in cleartext to any non-localhost http:// base URL.

fix: After float(v), reject non-finite values and enforce sane bounds (min_samples >= 1 integer; max_brier/max_ece/min_auc within [0,1]) with CalibrationError, mirroring the isfinite check already in _unit().
problem: resolve_policy() accepts any float for min_samples/max_brier/max_ece/min_auc with no finiteness or range validation. Python's json.loads accepts bare NaN, and every comparison against NaN is False, so a policy block containing NaN (or max_brier:1.0 / min_auc:0.0 / min_samples:-1) silently clears all four promotion checks and makes eligible_for_blocking true — a fail-open on the very gate that authorizes advisory->blocking promotion.

fix: Raise CalibrationError(f"{field} must be in [0,1]") when v is outside the range (allow a tiny float-noise epsilon), rather than max/min clamping.
problem: _unit() silently clamps out-of-range values into [0,1] instead of rejecting them. A labels file with outcome:2, or a producer bug emitting score:1.7 / -0.5, is coerced to the nearest legal value; clamping can only shrink the (score-outcome) gap, so malformed calibration data quietly improves Brier/ECE and pushes the report toward eligible-for-blocking.

fix: Catch OSError (superset of FileNotFoundError) in load_json and re-raise as CalibrationError so IO failures land on the documented exit 2.
problem: load_json() catches only FileNotFoundError and JSONDecodeError; other OSErrors from _read()'s open() (directory path, permission denied, unreadable mount) escape main()'s except (AssertionError, CalibrationError) as an uncaught traceback and the process exits 1. The header documents IO error as exit 2, and exit 1 is the --gate "NOT eligible for blocking" signal — a CI gate job cannot distinguish an unreadable input from a genuine not-eligible verdict.

fix: Factor the raw per-bin means into a helper that reliability() rounds for display and ece() consumes unrounded.
problem: ece() sums over reliability()'s rows, whose mean_score and empirical_rate are already round(...,4) display values. The gate metric is therefore derived from presentation-rounded numbers and silently changes if reliability()'s rounding is ever adjusted.

fix: Add --policy/--threshold flags (or read a policy object from the --labels file) and apply them on the join path too.
problem: The --scores/--labels join path hard-codes dict(DEFAULT_POLICY) and DEFAULT_THRESHOLD with no override, while the single-file path honours the input's "policy" and "threshold". docs/agent-rules/verifier-sidecar.md:101 documents the join as the end-to-end loop, so the recommended path cannot tune promotion thresholds at all.

fix: Wrap the record write in its own try/except OSError that warns to stderr without masking the in-flight exception, and validate the --record path before starting the run.
problem: The --record write sits in a finally block; if open(args.record,'w') fails (bad directory, read-only path) the OSError replaces whatever exception produce() raised and is not caught by main()'s except (AssertionError, ProduceError, FileNotFoundError), producing a traceback and exit 1 instead of the documented exit 2 — and the original produce failure is lost.

The global factory override (&MakeStubGated) and g_ui.showPreferences=true then leak into subsequent tests, and the still-in-flight worker/queued PublishProbeResult outlives the test — reintroducing exactly the teardown race this PR removed, just on the failure branch.

fix: Validate length too: `if len(fixed) != 1 or fixed not in LETTERS: raise EndpointError(...)`.
problem: `if fixed not in LETTERS` is a SUBSTRING test against the string "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRST", not a single-letter membership test. `--fixed ""`, `--fixed AB`, `--fixed CDE` all pass validation and then `LETTERS.index(fixed)` (line 85) silently resolves to the first letter of the run (empty string -> index 0 -> 'A'). The documented contract ("--fixed must be one of A-T", exit 2) is not enforced, so a typo'd demo/smoke run quietly pins the wrong letter instead of erroring.

fix: Read and discard Content-Length bytes before sending the 404 (or send `Connection: close` on the error path).
problem: The 404 branch of do_POST replies and returns WITHOUT draining the request body from self.rfile. With `protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"` (line 159) the connection is keep-alive, so the unread body bytes are re-parsed as the next request line, desyncing the connection (client sees a garbage 400/hang) for any POST to a wrong path that carries a payload — e.g. a caller pointing VERIFIER_BASE_URL at a base that yields /v1/v1/chat/completions.

fix: Add a trailing `except Exception as exc: self._send(500, {"error": {"message": str(exc)}})`.
problem: Only EndpointError is caught around parse_request/chat_completion. Any other exception (e.g. a non-dict `messages` element chain, or a TypeError from odd JSON shapes) escapes do_POST, so BaseHTTPRequestHandler aborts the connection instead of returning a 5xx — the client sees a connection reset rather than a diagnosable error.

fix: Use `run bash -c "set -o pipefail; ..."` in the piped tests.

A producer that dies mid-run (non-zero exit) is masked as long as the sidecar tolerates the truncated stream; same shape at lines 89, 95 and 107. fix: Only treat a single-letter dist as degenerate when the raw top_logprobs list itself was short/uninformative (e.g. pass the pre-filter token count into is_degenerate), or drop the len<2 rule and rely solely on the placeholder/flat-value checks.
problem: is_degenerate() treats len(dist) < 2 as degenerate, but `dist` is not the raw top_logprobs — extract_logprobs() filters it down to A-T letter tokens only. A healthy, highly confident backend whose top-20 contains just one letter token (remaining slots being whitespace/punctuation/word-piece variants) yields len(dist)==1, so --strict aborts the entire run with "backend returned degenerate logprobs" on a perfectly good response. The DeepSeek recipe added in the same PR puts --strict in the copy-paste command, making this the default path.

fix: Detect the placeholder pattern by magnitude/clustering instead of an absolute cut (e.g. require values far below -1000, or require the non-top values to be identical placeholders), and/or only warn rather than abort when the top token is itself a plausible logprob.
problem: `all(v <= _DEGENERATE_LOGPROB for v in values[1:])` with _DEGENERATE_LOGPROB = -100.0 flags a legitimate but very peaked distribution (e.g. A=-0.0001, B=-105) as degenerate; real logprobs can legitimately fall below -100 for a near-deterministic single-token answer. Under --strict this hard-fails a valid run.

fix: Bound the whole retry by a wall-clock deadline (e.g. give up after ~500ms total) instead of only an attempt count, and/or lower the per-attempt busy_timeout while retrying; alternatively make the UI-thread caller (UpdateCachedCommentCount) route the cache write off the render thread so no sleep_for ever runs on the main thread.

fix: Normalise before sorting, e.g. `paths = [p.replace(os.sep, "/") for p in glob.glob("agents/scripts/core/*.sh") + glob.glob("agents/scripts/core/lib/*.sh") + glob.glob("agents/scripts/project/*.sh")]` then `for path in sorted(paths):` and drop the in-loop replace (or `sorted(..., key=lambda p: p.replace(os.sep, "/"))`). problem: The embedded Python sorts the glob results BEFORE normalising path separators: `for path in sorted(glob(core/*.sh) + glob(core/lib/*.sh) + glob(project/*.sh))` (lines 104-106) and only then `path = path.replace(os.sep, "/")` (line 107). With a native Windows Python, glob returns `agents/scripts/core\\x.sh` and `agents/scripts/core/lib\\y.sh`; because '/' (0x2F) sorts before '\\' (0x5C), all 9 agents/scripts/core/lib/*.sh rows sort ahead of every agents/scripts/core/*.sh row, while the committed baseline (POSIX order) interleaves them at rows 28-36. Row ORDER is therefore platform-dependent and the line-by-line `diff -u` at line 139 reports drift.
scenario: Verified at HEAD on the Windows dev box (resolve_py -> /c/Python314/python): `bash agents/scripts/core/classify-layer-consumers.sh --check` prints 'classification DRIFTED' with a 200/200-row diff, although sorting both sides shows the row SET is identical (order-only drift). The failure text then calls it a 'REWIRE OBLIGATION' and says to re-run with --regen; a --regen on Windows rewrites the committed baseline in Windows order, after which every Linux / MSYS-python --check drifts instead. The plan's verification ledger uses `classify-layer-consumers.sh --check` as a PASS step, so the tool is unusable as evidence on the primary dev platform (non-gating, fails loud rather than open).

fix: Match against display text, not stored ids, and keep the predicate pure. Have ApplyGridFilterProjection (SmatchetActiveProjectGridTable.cpp:219), which already holds the catalog index, give TicketMatchesGridFilter a per-field view built once per rebuild. Skip fieldValues keys with no catalog field (drops Plane 'uuid' and '_smatchet_is_pr'). Then match the mapped name, and fall back to the raw value when no option id matches, as Jira option fields store text. problem: The full-text loop matches every raw fieldValues string, but for Plane those strings are hidden UUIDs. MapPlaneIdentityFields stores fieldValues["uuid"], an internal key with no catalog column (PlaneIssueMappingPure.cpp:117). MapPlaneWorkItemJsonToCachedTicket stores the State and Cycle values as ids: status is NestedDetailValue(issue,"state_detail","state","id") and sprint is NestedDetailValue(issue,"cycle_details","cycle","id") (PlaneIssueMappingPure.cpp:154/157). The grid shows names instead, via PlaneClient::ResolveDisplayValue (PlaneIssueMutation.cpp:257-275, called from TicketFieldEditor.cpp:1143). So in a Plane pane the filter matches text the user cannot see and misses the names the user can see. This breaks the header contract in TicketGridFilterPure.h:9-11 ('any displayable field value ... hidden ids/emails never match'). The GitHub sentinel _smatchet_is_pr="1" is a smaller case of the same leak.
scenario: Plane pane with rows in State 'In Progress' (state UUID such as 3fa85f64-...). (a) Typing 'In Progress', or a cycle name, matches no row by its State or Cycle column, although Jira, Linear and GitHub panes match status names after this PR. (b) Typing a word made only of hex letters or digits ('add', 'bed', 'face', '42') keeps every row whose own uuid, state UUID or cycle UUID contains that fragment. State and cycle UUIDs are shared, so a whole State bucket can match spuriously even though no visible cell contains the text.

scenario: On a Windows dev box with the Windows SDK and bats installed, running scripts/dev/test-all.sh (or test-release-signing-selectors-bats.sh) makes configure_signing return 0. A scratch repro on this host, using the test's exact env inputs with abs_path, resolve_signtool and configure_signing extracted from HEAD, returned rc=0 with SIGN_TOOL=/c/Program Files (x86)/Windows Kits/10/bin/10.0.26100.0/x64/signtool.exe. The script then dies later (ISCC, cmake or dirty tree), or, on a clean tree with Inno Setup installed, starts a real release build inside the bats run. The assertion [[ "$output" == *"Unable to locate signtool.exe"* ]] fails, so the wrapper exits 1 and test-all.sh is red.

problem: The reconcile listing `issue_listing=$(gh issue list ... --label plan-lock-stale ... 2>/dev/null || true)` throws away gh's stderr and exit status and prints no warning. The comment block at lines 240-242 says "a gh failure warns and the sweep still exits 0", but only the per-Issue close failure (line 291) warns. When the listing fails, the result is an empty heredoc, nothing is closed, and the final notice prints `closed=0`, which looks the same as "nothing to close".
scenario: In CI or a local git-janitor run, the label-scoped `gh issue list` call fails: rate limit, transient API/network error, or a token without issue-read scope. locks_authoritative=1, so the reconcile runs and gets an empty listing. No `::warning::` is emitted and the run reports closed=0. If the failure keeps happening, every resolved lock's Issue stays open forever again (the exact defect #2195 fixed) and nothing in the logs shows it.

fix: Correct the disclosure to say 'the call stacks and stack memory of every application thread'. Change the help-marker string (SmatchetBugReportUi.cpp:196-199) and PRIVACY.md:87-91. Also fix the matching comments: BugReportService.h:108, BugReportService.cpp:234, SmatchetBugReportUi.cpp:174, tools/bug-report-relay/README.md:96, src/index.js:80-82 and wrangler.toml:19-20. The other option is a MINIDUMP_CALLBACK that keeps only the faulting thread's stack, but that is a code change with a diagnostic cost.
problem: The in-product consent text says the minidump carries only 'the faulting thread's call stack' and 'the thread's own stack memory', and PRIVACY.md:87 says it 'captures the crashing thread's stack'. But both writers call MiniDumpWriteDump with kSmatchetDumpType (MiniDumpNormal|MiniDumpFilterModulePaths) and a null callback (SmatchetCrashHandler.cpp:132). MiniDumpNormal captures the stack memory of every thread in the process. The same TU's self-dump comment (SmatchetCrashHandler.cpp ~216) even says 'every thread's stack is still captured'. So the user agrees to a smaller scope than what actually gets uploaded.
scenario: A crash happens while sync/network worker threads are partway through requests, or while the UI thread holds text-input fragments. The user reads the help marker or PRIVACY.md, believes only the crashing thread's stack leaves the machine, and leaves 'Attach crash minidump' ticked (the default). The uploaded .dmp holds the stack memory of every thread: UI, sync workers and HTTP workers, including any stack-resident request or response fragments.

fix: Change the README table row, the 'global bucket' paragraph, the wrangler.toml comment and the index.js:59 comment to say the ceiling is per Cloudflare location and approximate. Point operators to the dashboard WAF rule (custom domain) or a Durable Object counter if they need a true relay-wide cap.
problem: Several places describe GLOBAL_RATE_LIMITER as 'the whole relay' bucket that 'stops a distributed flood (many IPs ...) from burning the GitHub token's secondary-rate-limit allowance': README.md:130 and 134-136, wrangler.toml:38-39 ('Whole-relay ceiling') and src/index.js:59. Cloudflare's rate-limit binding does not work that way. Its docs (Locality) say limits are 'local to the Cloudflare location that your Worker runs in', with a separate counter per key per location, and are 'permissive, eventually consistent'. The fixed key 'global' therefore gives 60/min per data center, not 60/min for the whole relay. The documented anti-flood guarantee does not hold.
scenario: A botnet spread across many regions hits POST /report. Each Cloudflare location allows up to 60 requests/min under the 'global' key, so the combined rate reaching GitHub issue-create is 60 x N locations. That easily exceeds GitHub's content-creation secondary limit (~80/min). The bot token gets throttled or flagged and legitimate bug reports fail, which is the exact outcome the README says this binding prevents.

fix: Add a CI step, e.g. `cd tools/bug-report-relay && node --test test/*.test.mjs` on Node >= 22. It needs no npm install, because the tests import only node: built-ins and ../src/index.js. A path filter on tools/bug-report-relay/** is enough.
problem: The new node:test suite (tools/bug-report-relay/test/index.test.mjs) checks the relay's fail-closed private-dump-repo gate and the rate limiters. No CI workflow or repo test runner calls it: no file under .github/ or scripts/ mentions bug-report-relay or 'node --test'. The only entry point is a manual `npm test` (README.md:164).
scenario: A later edit to isDumpRepoPrivate or handleReport makes the dump gate fail open, for example by caching negative answers inverted or by falling back to assetsRepo when visibility is unknown. The suite would catch it, but nothing runs the suite, so the regression merges green and the next manual `wrangler deploy` ships it.

fix: Do not write a stale whole image after draining. Add a locked migration helper: take GetConfigRmwMutexRef(), call DrainPendingTrackerLocked(), and skip writing cfg if a snapshot was drained (the snapshot came from the live object, so writing it already re-sealed or purged every secret through SaveSecretsAndPurgeLegacy). Otherwise re-read the pre-override disk image under the lock and write that. Do not switch to Update() as-is: LoadTrackerConfigForUpdate applies env overrides, so the migration would persist them, which the ordering note at lines 898-904 explicitly forbids.
problem: The legacy-secret migration re-save in LoadImpl calls ConfigManager::Save(cfg) with an image read from disk at line 838, before the RMW lock is taken. Since this PR, Save first drains the worker's queued UI snapshot and writes it, then writes this older disk image on top, which reverts the snapshot's edits. That breaks the contract this PR added at ConfigManager.h:877-879 ('A caller that builds its image from a fresh Load() must use Update() instead'). Before the PR the same overlap was a 50/50 race; now, whenever the slot is still full when the migration Save takes the lock, the revert always happens.
scenario: Win32 with DPAPI protection failing, so ApplySecretPersist keeps the plaintext fallback. This needs an MCP auth token or AI key configured. LoadSecretFields then sets migrate.McpAuthToken/AiApiKey on every cache-miss Load(), and every Save invalidates the cache, so the next Load() misses again. Sequence: the UI calls EnqueueTrackerConfig(S1); before the worker wakes, any thread (often the UI thread itself, later in the same frame) calls ConfigManager::Load(). Load reads the pre-S1 file, migrate.Any() is true, and Save(cfg) runs: DrainPendingTrackerLocked writes S1, then WriteTrackerConfigLocked(cfg) overwrites it with the pre-S1 image. On disk the user's edit is reverted until the next UI save, and it is lost if the app exits first. Not reachable on first launch after an upgrade, because the first Load migrates before the UI can enqueue anything.

fix: Either route these writers through a locked JSON read-modify-write seam in ConfigManager (take GetConfigRmwMutexRef(), call DrainPendingTrackerLocked(), then LoadMergedConfigJson, set the key, WriteConfigJson), or at minimum correct the doc to say Save is serialized against the ConfigManager Save/Update/SaveAnnotateAnalysis writers only and name the raw WriteConfigJson callers as unsequenced.
problem: The new Save doc says it is 'Serialized against every other config writer'. That is false at HEAD. Four raw-JSON read-modify-write writers call LoadMergedConfigJson() then WriteConfigJson() without GetConfigRmwMutexRef() and without draining the queued snapshot: config.set (BuiltinCommands_Config.cpp:209-211), tickets.monitor (BuiltinCommands_Config.cpp:282-284), the perf-window toggle (BuiltinCommands_Perf.cpp:217-218) and SaveLuaLayoutDebounced (Source/Plugins/LuaConsole/LuaConsolePlugin.cpp:44-46). WriteConfigJson only takes the IO mutex. So the #2191 lost-update class still applies to these writers, while the header tells future authors it is closed.
scenario: SaveLuaLayoutDebounced (UI thread, during a Lua-panel splitter drag) reads the merged JSON. The config-save worker then writes a queued snapshot S1 under the RMW lock. SaveLuaLayoutDebounced writes its JSON, read before S1 landed, and silently reverts S1's tracker keys on disk. config.set and tickets.monitor from an MCP/CLI thread have the same interleaving.

fix: Compare ASCII-case-insensitively (e.g. ToLowerAsciiCopy(ticket.id) == ToLowerAsciiCopy(key), with the key lowered once outside the loop) and call target.gridState.SetActiveIssue(ticket.id) so the canonical id is stored. Add a bucket-A or bucket-E case for a lowercase key on a loaded row.
problem: GridSearchJumpToTicket matches the typed key against the loaded snapshot with a case-sensitive `ticket.id == key`, but the classifier deliberately accepts a lowercase key as TicketKey (ExtractIssueKeyPrefix uses IsAsciiAlpha/IsAsciiAlphaNum; GridSearchInputClassifier.test.cpp:31 asserts "proj-7" is a key) and the live row filter (TicketMatchesGridFilter) is case-insensitive. A key typed in a different case therefore narrows the grid to the loaded row, yet Enter skips the in-grid jump and falls through to app.OpenUrl, which opens the system browser. The same applies to a GitHub key whose owner/repo case differs from FormatGitHubIssueKey's canonical form.
scenario: A Jira pane has SMAT-1 loaded. The user types "smat-1". The glyph shows the issue-key mode and the grid filters down to the SMAT-1 row. On Enter, applyGridSearchEnter sends it to GridSearchJumpToTicket, "SMAT-1" == "smat-1" is false, and OpenUrl(BuildIssueBrowseUrl(d.cfg, "smat-1")) opens an external browser tab instead of selecting the row that is on screen. That breaks the documented no-network loaded-row jump (SmatchetUI.h:468-473).

fix: Return TrimCopyAsciiWhitespace(pane.gridSearchBuf) from GridSearchRowFilterText, so the filter matches on the same text the classification used. Do this only when the trimmed text is non-empty; when it is empty, return an empty string, which means match everything.
problem: GridSearchRowFilterText returns the RAW box text (std::string(pane.gridSearchBuf)), but GridSearchFiltersRows and applyGridSearchEnter classify the TRIMMED text. TicketMatchesGridFilter does not trim (FoldAsciiCopy only folds case), so leading or trailing whitespace is part of the substring needle. A key pasted with a trailing space is classified TicketKey, filters rows, and then hides its own row. A whitespace-only box classifies as TitleSearch, which GridSearchInputClassifier.h:141 calls a no-op filter, yet it still filters the rows against the spaces.
scenario: The user pastes "SMAT-1 " (a double-click copy that picked up the trailing space) into the box. ClassifyGridSearchInput trims it to TicketKey and the row filter becomes active with needle "smat-1 ". The id "SMAT-1" does not contain that needle, so the grid shows "No issues match the filter." On Enter, the trimmed key is found and SetActiveIssue selects a row that the filter is hiding, so the user sees no result.

fix: Reword it to: true when the box text filters the loaded rows. That covers plain title words and a bare ticket key, which also jumps on Enter. A structured query never filters, because it commits on Enter.
problem: The comment on GridSearchFiltersRows says it is true only when the text reads as plain title words "rather than a ticket key or a structured query, which commit on Enter instead". The code says otherwise: AppliesAsRowFilter (GridSearchInputClassifier.h:164) returns true for TicketKey, GridSearchFiltersRows therefore returns true for a key, and grid_search_apply.test.cpp:254 asserts exactly that. The API contract in the comment contradicts the implementation and the tests.
scenario: A maintainer trusts the header comment and treats GridSearchFiltersRows()==true as meaning title-search mode. For example, they might show the title-search hint, or skip the key jump, whenever it holds. A ticket key is then routed the wrong way.

fix: Drop the parenthetical, or replace it with a self-contained note on why the guard exists.
problem: The comment cites "the same per-frame-alloc guard as the grid search box's mirror", but that mirror no longer exists. This PR removed the omnibox-to-filter-buffer mirror, and DrawGridSearchBox (SmatchetGridHeaderUi.cpp:288-315) writes straight into pane.gridSearchBuf with no string mirror. The cross-reference points at code that is gone.
scenario: A reader looks for the referenced grid-search mirror guard to see the pattern or keep the two in sync, and finds nothing.

fix: Run the pump on the mobile host once per frame, every frame (the desktop pumps unconditionally, not just when the grid is visible). In drawMobileShell, after the grid page and dock windows are submitted, compute readOnlyMode = d.cfg.ReadOnlyMode || app.GetTrackerConnectivityBannerForUi(nullptr).Kind == TrackerConnectivityBannerForUi::Level::Error and call PumpGridFieldEdits(app, d, readOnlyMode). Better still, extract one shared grid-host-tail helper (latch drain + edit pump) that both hosts call, so the mobile host cannot drift again. Add a headless test that forces EffectiveUiMode::Mobile, enqueues an edit through the embedded grid path, and asserts that d.queuedFieldEdits drains (hasInFlightEdit set or worker dispatched).
problem: This PR mirrored only part of drawGridPaneWindows' once-per-frame host tail onto the mobile host. drawEmbeddedFocusedGrid now drains the pane-action latch, but the field-edit pump that the same PR moved into the desktop-only tail (SmatchetGridPaneWindows.cpp:205-213, 'panes only ENQUEUE') still has no mobile caller. The embedded grid enqueues every cell edit: SmatchetActiveProjectGridUi.cpp:298 EnqueueGridFieldEdits, with no embedded gate on allowEditsForCell, plus the TicketFieldEditor long-press and Save path built for touch. In Mobile mode, SmatchetUI.cpp:391-398 returns before drawSecondaryWindows, which holds the only drawGridPaneWindows call (SmatchetUI.cpp:1205). PumpGridFieldEdits' only other caller is the perf.grid_edit_pump command. So d.queuedFieldEdits is never popped while in Mobile mode.
scenario: On an Android phone (Auto resolves Mobile), the user long-presses a grid cell, changes Status and taps Save. RenderFieldCell pushes a PendingFieldEdit and EnqueueGridFieldEdits appends it to d.queuedFieldEdits. No pump runs, so no worker starts, there is no PUT and no CommitOrQueue SQLite offline-queue write, and no Saving chip appears. The cell shows the old snapshot value. The edit lives only in memory: quitting the app while in Mobile loses it, which also breaks Pillar 6's rule that offline writes persist to the queue. On a desktop window auto-resolved to Mobile (narrow), the queued edits fire minutes or hours later, the first time a Desktop frame runs drawGridPaneWindows. That is the same stale-replay hazard this PR's comment at lines 219-222 describes for the latch.

fix: Emit one tab-joined row by wrapping the projection: `--query "[[appId,password,tenant]]" -o tsv`. Or keep the query and read three lines: `{ IFS= read -r CLIENT_ID; IFS= read -r CLIENT_SECRET; IFS= read -r TENANT_ID; } <<<"$CREDS_TSV"`. Add a bats case that stubs `az` with real knack-shaped output (one value per line) so the parse is regression-tested.
problem: Credential parse never succeeds. `az ... --query "[appId,password,tenant]" -o tsv` (line 169) returns a top-level flat list of three strings, and az's TSV formatter (knack format_tsv) writes each top-level list item as its own row. That is the same output shape as the common `--query "[].name" -o tsv` one-value-per-line idiom. So CREDS_TSV is three newline-separated lines, not one tab-separated line. `IFS=$'\t' read -r CLIENT_ID CLIENT_SECRET TENANT_ID <<<"$CREDS_TSV"` reads only line 1, so CLIENT_SECRET and TENANT_ID stay empty.
scenario: Any run that gets past the preconditions: create-for-rbac creates the app registration, service principal, client secret and Signer role assignment. Line 175 then finds CLIENT_SECRET empty, and line 176 dies with 'could not parse the credential' while set -e is still on. The one-time secret is never printed, the Reader-on-account assignment never runs, and the endpoint/gh-variable block is never shown. This is exactly the stranded-secret outcome the comment at lines 178-181 says must not happen. A re-run is blocked by the duplicate-name guard (line 150), so the operator has to finish everything by hand. The script that SIGNING.md:170-178 documents as the setup path cannot complete.

fix: Near the top, after argument parsing, add `export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`. The script only calls az and coreutils, so a global export is safe. Alternatively, wrap az with `az() { MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 command az "$@"; }`. Also make sure the manual-recovery command printed at line 211 works when pasted into Git Bash, for example by prefixing it with MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1.
problem: Every ARM resource ID passed to az starts with `/subscriptions/...`: `--ids` at lines 133 and 217, `--scopes` at line 167, `--scope` at line 203. Under Git Bash (the repo's Windows shell for scripts/publish), `az` resolves to the Azure CLI wbin shim, which runs the native python.exe, and MSYS rewrites any argument that looks like an absolute POSIX path. I checked this with the same argument shape in this tree: `python -c 'import sys;print(repr(sys.argv[1]))' /subscriptions/0000/resourceGroups/rg/providers/...` prints 'C:/Program Files/Git/subscriptions/0000/...'. With MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 the argument stays intact. The script has no guard, while its sibling release-github.sh already guards native calls with `native_exec` (MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1) after the #1957 postmortem on this same class.
scenario: A maintainer on Windows runs `az login` and then `bash scripts/publish/setup-trusted-signing-sp.sh --resource-group rg --account acct --profile prof` from Git Bash, as SIGNING.md:174-178 shows. verify_resource sends a mangled `C:/Program Files/Git/subscriptions/...` ID. az rejects it as an invalid resource ID, which does not match the not-found regex, so the script reports 'could not verify the signing account' and asks to continue. If the operator confirms (the script presents an inconclusive check as benign) or passed --yes, create-for-rbac gets a mangled --scopes value and fails with the misleading 'If it rejected the role name' message, possibly after the app and secret already exist. The Reader assignment and the accountUri read are mangled the same way. The script cannot complete on Git Bash.

fix: Rewrite lines 21-24: the toggles save automatically with the view (debounced autosave, no Unsaved strip / Discard); keep the sentence about the `story_group_sort` / `hide_parents` keys in smatchet_views.json.
problem: Doc-vs-code drift: the guide says flipping Parent group / Hide parent stories marks the view as changed and raises the 'Unsaved layout changes' strip with Save / Save as new... / Discard. At HEAD the toggles are autosaved (column-view-save-simplification): DrawSortByPopupBody (Source/Core/src/Ui/SmatchetGridHeaderUi.cpp:176-183) only arms d.viewLayoutSaveAt and never sets d.viewsDirty, and drawActiveProjectUnsavedStrip (Source/Core/src/Ui/SmatchetActiveProjectGridUi.cpp:543-553) states layout edits incl. hide-parents/story-group 'can no longer appear here'; the strip is now query-only ('Query changed but not saved'). The bucket-E test also asserts !g_ui.viewsDirty after each toggle.
scenario: A user follows the guide, flips Hide parent stories expecting to Discard it later; no strip appears and the change is already persisted to smatchet_views.json, so there is no Discard path as documented.

fix: Drop the keyboard-shortcuts bullet, or re-describe it generically (e.g. 'for app-wide shortcuts'); point view creation at the CLI Guide's view.* commands instead.
problem: The Related link describes docs/guides/keyboard-shortcuts.md as covering 'the view-apply and view-create shortcuts used alongside the Sort By popup', but that guide documents no view-apply or view-create shortcut (only sidebar/panel/tool toggles and command-palette keys); view.create exists only as a CLI command (Source/Core/src/Commands/ViewCommands.cpp:189).
scenario: A reader follows the link looking for view apply/create shortcuts and finds none.

fix: Rewrite the help text at lines 48-51 (and the line-45 tooltip) to match HEAD behaviour. Suggested wording: after each sync, missing parents are fetched, following the chain up to 16 levels with one request per level, and the children of the view's own rows are fetched too. Turning it off skips both, so children of a missing parent show as top-level rows and descendants the query did not match are not loaded. Keep it in line with docs/guides/parent-hierarchy.md 'How missing parents are loaded' and 'How missing children are loaded'.
problem: The in-app help marker for Preferences -> Editing -> Grid behaviour -> 'Load parent issues' says missing parents 'are fetched in one extra request' and (line 50) 'Turn off to skip that request'. That was true when this line landed (2026-09-07), but #2223 made the ancestor fetch chase up to kMaxParentFetchHops=16 hops (one request per hop) and #2225 put the downward children fetch (FetchChildrenIntoQueue, up to kMaxChildFetchHops=16 hops) behind the same cfg.LoadParentIssues switch (Source/Core/src/Sync/TicketSyncService.cpp:937 and :1015). Those PRs updated docs/guides/parent-hierarchy.md (lines 49-53, 93-94) but not this in-app text or the tooltip at line 45, so the help now understates the cost and omits that the switch also turns off descendant loading.
scenario: A user with a narrow view such as `key = EPIC-1` reads the help, which describes one parent request, and turns 'Load parent issues' off to save that request. On the next sync the children fetch is skipped as well (TicketSyncService.cpp:1015), so the view shows only the epic row and the story/task/subtask tree is gone. The help text never mentioned that.

fix: Reorder step 3 so the clear is observed from a populated state: click kHideParentsRef OFF first (Parent group still ON), YieldUntil cachedDepths.size() == ticketCount and IM_CHECK that it repopulated, then click kStoryGroupRef OFF and YieldUntil cachedDepths.empty() (keep the autosave-armed / !viewsDirty / filteredIndices checks after each click). Update the header item 3 and the step-3 comment to match.
problem: The step-3 'both OFF clears the depth cache' assertion (depthsClearedAgain) is vacuous: step 2 (Parent group ON + Hide parents ON) already leaves pane.cachedDepths empty (SmatchetActiveProjectGridTable.cpp:336-337 clears it when hideParents is set), and with storyGroupSort OFF no branch ever writes depths, so cachedDepths.empty() is already true before either step-3 click. YieldUntil returns true on its first yielded frame regardless of what the both-OFF projection branch does. The file header (item 3) and the in-test comment ('depth cache drains') claim this pins the ON->OFF clear, but the test never turns Parent group OFF while depths are populated.
scenario: A regression drops pane.cachedDepths.clear() from the both-OFF else-branch (SmatchetActiveProjectGridTable.cpp:344-346). In the real app a user toggles Parent group ON (depths populated) then OFF; stale depths remain and the flat grid draws rows indented via ctx.currentRowDepth (SmatchetActiveProjectGridTable.cpp:1090). This test still passes, because at step 3 the cache was already empty from step 2's hide-parents flatten.

fix: Only count human `@coderabbitai review` comments made for this head. Add `.created_at` to the --jq projection and keep only comments created after the head's CodeRabbit StatusContext `createdAt` (already in the GraphQL rollup) or after the head's push time. Older asks should fall through to the terminal `post failure "OSS <10 stars ..."`.
problem: The OSS manual-trigger arm's human_asked scan covers every issue comment on the PR, not just comments for the current head. Once any human has posted `@coderabbitai review` (on any earlier head), every later head that CodeRabbit marks 'manual review required' takes the `return 1` wait path. The poll window then runs out and the action posts `pending "awaiting CodeRabbit review on current head"`. That is the silent, unbounded pending this PR set out to replace with a terminal failure.
scenario: OSS repo under 10 stars. A human comments `@coderabbitai review` on head A and CR reviews A. The author pushes head B, and CR posts `Review skipped: manual review required for this OSS repository` on B (the repo's own process 2026-08-30 entry says this happens on every head, observed after each push on #2176). On the synchronize run, decide() reaches the OSS arm and finds head A's human comment, so it sets human_asked=true and returns 1 on every poll. After POLL_BUDGET_SECONDS it posts pending on the required `CR findings (0 actionable)` context, and nothing re-triggers it. The PR is stuck with no terminal failure naming the waive/trigger moves.

fix: Scope the dedup to the current head. Count an existing ask only if its body has `cr-human-first-review-nudge:<head>`, or if its `createdAt` (add it to the GraphQL comments selection) is later than the head commit's push/committed time. Otherwise post a new trigger.
problem: The 'human already asked, do not double-post' check counts any human `@coderabbitai review` among the PR's last 40 comments, whatever head it was posted for. The script stamps its own comment with a per-head marker (`cr-human-first-review-nudge:<head>`) but never checks for it. After one human trigger, the sanctioned helper prints 'human @coderabbitai review already on PR - waiting' and exits 0 on every later head, so it never posts the trigger that the new head needs.
scenario: Head A was triggered (by this script or by hand) and CR reviewed it. The author pushes head B, and CR again waits for a manual request. The operator, or the agent following the merge-gates.sh first-poll INFO tip / ship-loops.md, runs `bash scripts/dev/trigger-coderabbit-review.sh <pr>`. on_head is 0 because there is no CR review on B, but human_nudge is 1 because of the head-A comment. The script exits 0 with 'waiting for CodeRabbit' and posts nothing. Combined with the action's matching PR-wide check, the PR stays pending until someone comments by hand or applies the waiver.

fix: Put the label/body waiver check in a function and call it inside decide() on every poll (or at least right before the final `post pending` / `post failure`), posting the override success and exiting if the waiver is now present.
problem: The waiver check runs once, at the start of the run, before the poll loop. Statuses are last-write-wins, and the workflow deliberately has no concurrency group. So a run that was already polling when the waiver labels were applied will post `pending`/`failure` after the `labeled` run has posted `success`, and that overwrites the waiver. The surviving comment's promise that 'applying the pair is enough - no manual gh run rerun' fails in exactly the busy-CR situation where the waiver is used.
scenario: CR is rate limited on a fresh head. The synchronize run, or the run started by CR's rate-limit comment, sits in the rate-limit `return 1` arm for up to 180 s. The human_asked wait arm added here also polls the full window. Within that window the operator or agent applies `cr-out-of-band` + `cr-disposition:...` (ship-loops.md section on rate-limited/silent CR). The labeled run posts success. Then the earlier run reaches window exhaustion and posts `pending "awaiting CodeRabbit review on current head"` on the required context. merge-gates.sh discounts it locally, but native `--auto` / branch protection still sees a pending required check. The waiver is inert again until someone runs a manual re-run, which is the tooling 2026-08-18 symptom.

fix: Add `edited` to the pull_request types (the run is cheap and idempotent). Or document in merge-gates.md:91 that a body marker must be in place before the label is applied, or else needs a manual re-run.
problem: The playbook (merge-gates.md:91) says the disposition can be a label OR a PR-body marker, and that the workflow 're-runs on labeled / unlabeled and posts success'. But `edited` is not in the pull_request types. A body-marker disposition added after the `cr-out-of-band` label triggers no re-run, so the waiver stays inert. This is the label-inert-until-rerun gap the PR closes for labels only.
scenario: The operator applies `cr-out-of-band` alone. The action logs 'cr-out-of-band present but no cr-disposition:<reason> label/body marker - override not honoured' and keeps the failure/pending. Following that hint, the operator adds `cr-disposition: cr-auto-review-disabled` to the PR body. No workflow run fires because the body edit is a pull_request `edited` event. The required `CR findings (0 actionable)` context keeps its old non-success value until a manual `gh run rerun`.

fix: Use one predicate everywhere: change 10-gate-filter.sh:77 and safe-admin-merge.sh:288/475 to `cr-disposition:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]<]` and the jq label test to require a non-empty suffix. Ideally keep the regex in one shared place, and add a selftest/bats case where the body `cr-disposition:<reason>` does NOT count.
problem: The three layers do not accept the same cr-disposition body marker, although action.yml:256-258 says they mirror each other. The action uses `cr-disposition:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]<]`, which rejects the doc placeholder `cr-disposition:<reason>`. safe-admin-merge.sh:288/475 (new here) and 10-gate-filter.sh:77 use `[^[:space:]]`, which accepts it. The label forms differ too: the action requires `^cr-disposition:.+` while the jq side accepts a bare `cr-disposition:` label.
scenario: A gate-area PR whose body quotes the playbook text `cr-out-of-band + a cr-disposition:<reason> attestation` gets only the `cr-out-of-band` label. The action refuses the override and keeps the required `CR findings` context red. merge-gates.sh downgrades gate 2, discounts the context, and reports GATES_PASSED. safe-admin-merge also discounts the red required context and allows an admin merge. So the PR-3 'recorded reason' attestation is met by placeholder text, and the layers disagree, so native auto-merge stalls while the admin path goes through.

fix: Give each Preferences edit row a stable identity. fix: Add --full-history to the git log in audit_delta (parity with seed-audit-sweep.py's range), i.e. `git -C "$repo" log --oneline --full-history "$pin..HEAD" -- ...`. This only makes the guard stricter.
problem: The phase-3 publication-audit freshness guard (audit_delta) runs `git log --oneline "$pin..HEAD" -- <specs>` with git's DEFAULT history simplification, which prunes side branches whose merge is TREESAME to a parent for the given paths. The sweep it is supposed to trigger (seed-audit-sweep.py) deliberately uses --full-history for exactly this reason, and filter-repo keeps every commit regardless. So post-pin side-branch commits that touched a manifest path but net to zero (add-then-remove inside a PR branch, or a merge resolved to the first parent's version) are invisible to the guard, which then reports the audit current while the rewritten history still publishes their content.
scenario: Verified in a sandbox repo: pin commit; side branch commits 'add token=leak' then 'remove leak' to agents/core/a.md; develop gets an unrelated commit; `git merge --no-ff side`. `git log --oneline pin..HEAD -- agents/core/ ':(exclude)x.md'` prints nothing, while the same command with --full-history lists both side commits. develop does take real merge commits (11 since 2026-08-01, e.g. 'Merge pull request #2202' on 2026-09-09). Phase 3 would pass 'publication audit is current' and filter-repo would publish the never-swept leak commit; phase-4b gitleaks only backstops credential shapes, not hosts, personal data or third-party text.
