fix: In the failure branch, mark the session as not authoritative for pruning, e.g. `summary.FullSyncCompleted = false;`. This follows the existing partial-result precedent in GitHubIssueSearch.cpp:368, and it makes SeedStaleDeletionForSession and ConvergeActiveTicketsToSessionKeepSet skip pruning while streamed rows still apply. Keep the error kind: when fetched.error().IsRetryable(), route the failure to the transient path instead of a non-transient caveat. Apply the same change to the failure branch in FetchChildrenIntoQueue (L1046-1055). Add a test that pre-caches an ancestor, fails the keyed fetch with TrackerErrorTransport, and asserts the cached ancestor is still there.
problem: When a keyed ancestor fetch fails at any hop, the failure branch (L968-977) only appends a soft summary.Warning and returns. It drops the TrackerError kind (it reads only .Detail) and leaves summary.FullSyncCompleted true. RunStreamingWorkerBody (L863-870) then marks every cached ticket that is not in workerKeepIds as stale. So every ancestor an earlier successful sync cached, but this sync could not re-fetch, is deleted from SQLite (DrainStaleDeletionBudget L351) and pruned from the grid (ConvergeActiveTicketsToSessionKeepSet). This breaks the Pillar 6 rule that a failed fetch never wipes cached data. The multi-hop loop widens the purge from level-1 parents to the whole ancestor chain. A Transport-kind outage on the hop is also reported as a non-transient 'Sync completed with a caveat' instead of the transient cached-data path.
scenario: Sync 1 is online and caches SUBTASK-1 -> TASK-1 -> STORY-1 -> EPIC-1. On sync 2 the Jira stream ends cleanly (FullSyncCompleted=true per JiraIssueSearch.cpp:487), but the hop-1 keyed request for STORY-1 times out, gets a 429 or 5xx, or the network drops between requests. STORY-1 and EPIC-1 are not in workerKeepIds, so they go into BackgroundStaleIds and are deleted from the cache and removed from ActiveTickets. The tree loses its upper levels. If the user then goes offline, those ancestors stay missing from the offline cache until a later sync succeeds. A hop-0 failure purges TASK-1, STORY-1 and EPIC-1 the same way. The existing test 'surfaces a soft warning when the parent fetch fails' (tests/Core/TicketSyncService.test.cpp:1088) never pre-caches the parent, so it cannot catch this.

fix: Change the comment and docs/guides/parent-hierarchy.md:51-53 to say that levels past the cap are not loaded in any sync, and drop the 'cyclic' reason. Add a LOG_WARN, or a summary.Warning, when the loop ends because hop reached kMaxParentFetchHops with currentRefs still pending.
problem: Two places claim that levels past the hop cap load on the next sync: the kMaxParentFetchHops comment (L915-917, 'A chain deeper than this still resolves — the remainder surfaces on the next sync') and docs/guides/parent-hierarchy.md:51-53 ('resolves the remaining levels on the next sync'). Both are false. Every sync restarts the chase from the streamed rows' parent refs with a fresh per-worker workerKeepIds (L827-828). Each sync therefore walks the same first 16 levels, and levels past kMaxParentFetchHops are never fetched. Hitting the cap also exits the loop silently, with no log or warning. The 'cyclic data' reasoning is also wrong: a cycle already stops early through the workerKeepIds dedup and never reaches 16 hops.
scenario: Take a parent chain more than 16 levels deep above a streamed leaf (pathological or malformed tracker data). Every sync fetches levels 1-16 and stops. Level 17 and above never appear, and a copy cached by another path is stale-purged on the next full sync. No log line records the cut, which contradicts the self-healing behaviour the docs describe.

fix: Treat an incomplete descendant walk as partial for stale-purge purposes. FetchChildrenIntoQueue should report incompleteness on the error branch and on the hop/page-cap exits (bool return or summary flag), and RunStreamingWorkerBody should then skip the localStaleIds computation for that sync (or clear FullSyncCompleted). Alternatively, retain cached tickets whose ParentKeyOf chain reaches a kept id. Add a TicketSyncService test: sync 1 caches a child; sync 2 runs with SetFetchChildrenOfKeysError(TrackerErrorTransport(...)); the child must still be in the cache and in ActiveTickets. The ancestor-fetch failure branch (:968-977, a different commit) has the same shape, so fix both together. Correct the 'surface on the next sync' comments.
problem: When the children fetch fails, FetchChildrenIntoQueue only appends a warning and returns. summary.FullSyncCompleted stays true, so RunStreamingWorkerBody (:861-885) marks as stale every cached id that is not in workerKeepIds. Descendants that an earlier sync's children pass cached, and that the view's own filter does not match, are not in workerKeepIds. SeedStaleDeletionForSession/DrainStaleDeletionBudget then DeleteTicket them from SQLite, and ConvergeActiveTicketsToSessionKeepSet removes them from the grid. A transient fetch failure therefore wipes cached data (Pillar 6), which contradicts the header/guide claim that the tickets fetched so far still apply. Truncation by kMaxChildFetchHops or Jira's kMaxPagesPerBatch cap does the same thing. Each sync restarts the walk from the streamed set, so the comment that the remaining descendants 'surface on the next sync' (TicketSyncService.cpp:920-925, JiraIssueSearch.cpp:633-636/694-696) is wrong: they are pruned on every sync.
scenario: View `key = EPIC-1`, Load parent issues on. Sync 1 succeeds and caches STORY-1/TASK-1/SUBTASK-1 as children. In sync 2 the streamed fetch succeeds (FullSyncCompleted=true), then FetchChildrenOfKeys returns a Transport error (timeout/429/5xx). workerKeepIds={EPIC-1} while GetAllTicketIds returns all four, so the three descendants become BackgroundStaleIds and are deleted from the cache and the grid. The grid drops to one row with a 'Sync completed with a caveat' banner. If the user then goes offline, the descendant tree is gone from the offline cache.

fix: Move a `queriedParents` set outside the hop loop and request only keys not yet queried in this sync. Children cached by earlier syncs should still be candidate parents, as the existing comment requires. At the top of every hop, before the network call, check `activeStreamingSync_.RequestId != reqId || activeStreamingSync_.Cancelled` under QueueMutex, the same per-hop check FetchMissingParentsIntoQueue does. Add a unit test where the streamed set already contains the whole tree and assert FetchChildrenOfKeysCallCount() == 1.
problem: The child-hop loop has two gaps. First, it deduplicates only within a hop: `seen` is reset every iteration, and every fetched child goes into the next hop, including tickets already queried as parents in an earlier hop (every streamed id is one). Second, the RequestId/Cancelled check only runs inside `if (!newChildren.empty())`. When the view's result set already contains the children, every hop re-queries keys it has already asked about and re-downloads the same issues (fields + expand=changelog). Nothing new is queued, and cancellation is never checked.
scenario: View `project = X` streams 4000 issues in an epic->story->subtask hierarchy. Hop 0 sends ~100 `parent in` requests that return ~3800 issues already present, so newChildren is empty and cancellation is not checked. Hop 1 sends ~95 requests that re-query stories and subtasks already queried in hop 0. Hop 2 sends ~50 more before a hop comes back empty. That is ~245 requests per sync, against ~40 for the streamed fetch itself. With cross-hop dedupe the walk would stop after hop 0. If the user switches views meanwhile (SyncWithBackend sets Cancelled and defers), the new sync waits for every remaining hop. ~AppController and RecreateLocalCacheDatabase call CancelAndJoinActiveStreamingSync on the UI thread and block for the rest of the walk.

fix: Add a blocking CI step, or a scripts/dev driver wired into the jira-fixture job, that runs UI_TEST_FILTER=GridParentHierarchyDeepChain with SMATCHET_TEST_JIRA_BACKEND_FIXTURE=tests/fixtures/jira_backend/parent-hierarchy-grid.json. Optionally, make the test fail an IM_CHECK instead of skipping when the fixture env names parent-hierarchy-grid.json but the PH-* keys are missing.
problem: GridParentHierarchyDeepChain/DeepChain_DepthsAndOrderMatchAncestry only runs its assertions when pointed at parent-hierarchy-grid.json, and no CI lane or driver script does that. The bucket-E `ui_test.run --all` lane (build-and-test.yml ~:1497) sets no SMATCHET_TEST_JIRA_BACKEND_FIXTURE, so BootSyncPrimaryLive skips. The jira-fixture lane (~:1762) runs test-ui-jira-deterministic-backend.sh with the default filter `JiraDeterministic` and basic-grid.json. The test logs SKIP and counts as passed in every lane, so the deep-chain UI coverage this PR advertises never runs.
scenario: A regression in how the live grid wires ComputeDepths/StoryGroupOrder for a multi-level chain (wrong cachedDepths, or a descendant ordered before its ancestor) passes CI, because the test returns at :250, or BootSyncPrimaryLive returns nullptr, in every lane.

fix: Accumulate into a local std::vector<TrackerUser> inside FetchUsers and move or swap it into outUsers only after reachedEnd is true and the list is sorted. Every false return then leaves outUsers empty (outUsers.clear() already runs at entry), and the explicit clear at line 118 becomes redundant. Add a JiraUserAndMetaHttp test where startAt=0 returns 1000 rows and startAt=1000 returns HTTP 500 (and a second case returning a non-JSON 200 body). Assert CHECK_FALSE(ok), CHECK(out.empty()) and that err names the failure.
problem: FetchUsers' in-loop early returns (non-200 at line 58, ParseBounded error at 68, non-array at 73, std::exception catch at 97) return false while outUsers still holds every user accumulated from the earlier, successful pages. Only the kMaxPages-exhaustion path (line 113-118) clears outUsers, although the PR's own comment at 114-117 says this contract (an empty roster on failure) is what the caller relies on. FetchFieldCatalog (TrackerFieldCatalog.cpp:390-416) ignores the bool except to set Warning. When users is non-empty it overwrites every user-type field's AllowedValues/AllowedValueOptions and sets outCatalog.Users. SmatchetUI.cpp:1533-1534 then calls SetAvailableUsers and SaveAvailableUsersForOfflineAsync, which UpsertLookups the non-empty payload over the persisted offline roster. Before this PR the single call left outUsers empty on any failure, so no partial roster could be published.
scenario: The org has more than 1000 users and a complete roster is already cached offline. On the next catalog refresh, page 1 (startAt=0) returns 200 with 1000 users. Page 2 then fails: a 429 or 5xx, a transport failure (status 0) when the network drops mid-fetch, or a captive portal or proxy returning a 200 HTML body that fails ParseBounded. FetchUsers returns false with 1000 users in outUsers. The truncated roster becomes the assignee/reporter dropdown options and the JQL autocomplete user list. It also overwrites the complete cached offline roster. This is the 'not all users loaded' symptom the PR was fixing, now persisted, and it breaks Pillar 6: a failed fetch is cached as final.

fix: Make the ids depend on the request offset, e.g. id = "a" + req.get_param_value("startAt") + "_" + std::to_string(i), with a named httplib::Request& parameter. Every page then contributes 1000 unique users and the comments become true. Otherwise, correct the comments to say the same 1000 ids repeat and only 1,000 rows accumulate.
problem: The page-bound test's comments say it discards an 'accumulated 50,000-row partial roster' (line 186) and serves '50 pages of 1000 rows each, all unique accountIds this time' (line 189). The handler at line 173 ignores the request, so every page has the same ids a0..a999. FetchUsers' seenAccountIds dedup keeps only 1,000 rows, so the test never exercises a 50,000-row accumulation, and the comments misstate what the test covers.
scenario: A maintainer reads the test as proof that the bound-exhaustion path handles 50,000 unique accumulated users. It only ever builds a 1,000-user roster after the first page, because pages 2 through 50 are all duplicates.

fix: In both guard branches, set a user-facing soft warning on the summary, for example summary.Warning = "Jira result size exceeded 100 MB; remaining issues not fetched. Narrow your view JQL." (append with '; ' if a warning is already set). Do the same in the count guard. Then either read the two flags or delete them. The pre-existing page-cap branch at 400-402, which only logs, can share the same Warning so every Jira truncation is reported.
problem: The Jira cumulative-size guard (and the result-count guard at 378) stop pagination silently. They LOG_WARN and set result.totalSizeLimitHit / result.resultCountLimitHit (declared at 310-311), but nothing ever reads those flags. They never set summary.Warning or summary.FetchError. The sync therefore takes the success path with no caveat, while GitHub's identical guard (GitHubIssueSearch.cpp:289) and Plane's page cap (PlaneIssueSearch.cpp:385) both surface a warning.
scenario: A Jira Cloud view with about 5000 issues is fetched with expand=changelog. Each page holds 100 issues, and the average page is above about 2 MB, which is about 20 KB per issue. That is routine for long histories or ADF descriptions, and stays under the 4 MB ParseBounded per-page cap. After about 40 pages the 100 MB total is crossed. The page that crosses it is thrown away and the remaining pages are never fetched. FullSyncCompleted is false, but Warning and FetchError are both empty, so TicketSyncService::ApplyIssueFetchPack / TickStreamingApply take the plain success branch with no 'Sync completed with a caveat' banner. The user sees roughly 3900 of 5000 issues with no sign the list is cut short. Extreme case: if page 1 alone is over 100 MB, this used to produce a parse FetchError that the user saw. Now the result is silently empty, and JiraDiagnoseZeroIssueResult sends an extra /myself request and logs a misleading 'API returned 0 issues for your JQL' warning.

fix: Mirror the page-cap branch. Build a warning string (for example "Plane total result size exceeded 100 MB; remaining issues not fetched. Narrow your view."), LOG_WARN it, and assign or append it to summary.Warning in both the size guard (404-411) and the count guard (440-446). Then read or delete the write-only TotalSizeLimitHit / ResultCountLimitHit fields.
problem: The Plane cumulative-size guard (and the result-count guard at 440) end pagination with EndedCleanly=false but never set summary.Warning. In the same loop, the outer page-cap branch at 378-386 explicitly sets summary.Warning so the UI shows a caveat for partial data. TotalSizeLimitHit / ResultCountLimitHit (347-348) are set but never read.
scenario: A Plane project's work-items, with expand=assignees,labels,state and large description_html, average more than 2 MB per 100-item page. That is still under the 4 MB ParseBounded cap. The 100 MB total is crossed before the 50-page cap, so the loop breaks with no warning. FetchIssuesStreamedImpl sets FullSyncCompleted=false with empty Warning and FetchError, and TicketSyncService reports a plain success. The user sees a truncated issue list with no 'Sync completed with a caveat' banner. If the 50-page cap had been hit instead, they would have seen the banner.

fix: Either delete the test and its tests/CMakeLists.txt entry (lines 570-573), or move the guard constants into one shared header (for example Source/Core/include/Tracker/SearchFetchGuards.h) that all three backends and the test include. Assert relationships against the real symbols, and reference smatchet::json_safe::kDefaultMaxBytes for the per-response limit. Ideally add a behavioural test that runs a page loop over a fake transport and checks it stops and warns. Separately, remove the result-count guards or justify them, since they are dead under the current page caps.
problem: The test is a tautology. It re-declares its own copies of the guard constants in an anonymous namespace (lines 12-27) and asserts them against the same literals. It includes no production header, and tests/CMakeLists.txt:572 confirms no production .cpp is linked. The real constants are function-local in JiraIssueSearch.cpp:327-329 and PlaneIssueSearch.cpp:367-369, and file-scope in GitHubIssueSearch.cpp:39-40. So the test can never fail: removing or changing a production guard still passes. Its own invariant (kXMaxPages * 100 < kXMaxResultCount, lines 41/52/63) also shows that all three result-count guards are unreachable, since the page caps bound the count below the count cap. kPerResponseMaxBytes duplicates json_safe::kDefaultMaxBytes instead of referencing it.
scenario: Someone deletes the Jira 100 MB guard or changes kGitHubMaxTotalFetchBytes to 500 MB. JqlSearchGuards.test.cpp still passes, so the suite gives false assurance that the memory-exhaustion guards exist and have the documented values.

fix: Replace `std::string RawBody` (PlaneIssueSearch.cpp:213) with `size_t RawBodyBytes = 0;`. Set it to response.text.size() at line 247 and add page.RawBodyBytes at line 403.
problem: FetchPlaneIssuePage copies the entire HTTP response body into out.RawBody only so RunPlanePageLoop can read page.RawBody.size() at line 403. Nothing else reads RawBody. The copy is made on every page, including error and oversized bodies, and stays alive for the whole loop iteration next to response.text, the BOM-stripped bodyForJson copy, and the parsed DOM. A guard added to limit memory adds one more full-body copy per page.
scenario: Every Plane sync page, including a 4 MB page or an oversized error body, allocates and holds an extra copy the size of the body on the sync worker. This raises peak memory per page for no benefit.

fix: Only commit an actual drag. Build renderedOrder from columns[i].Key in index order. Return early when visualOrder == renderedOrder, because then no drag happened and nothing should be written. Also skip the whole write-back (width and order) when columns[] is stale relative to the live view: either the renderable subset of activeView.Columns keys != renderedOrder, or ViewState.GetRevision() != gridFrameCtx_.viewsRevision. The next frame rebuilds columns[] from the new revision. Add a bucket-E test: reorder in the Columns tab, Apply, then assert the grid and the saved view keep the new order after a few frames.
problem: CaptureHeaderDragColumnOrder treats any difference between the table's visual order (built from this frame's columns[]) and the LIVE active view's Columns as a header drag, then rewrites the view to the visual order (ReorderViewColumns, BumpRevision, autosave). columns[] comes from the per-frame cache that drawViewStateAndConnectivity builds at frame start (keyed on the frame-start ViewState revision, SmatchetUI.cpp:828-845; resolvePaneColumns reuses it), but drawSecondaryWindows draws the Views dashboard (SmatchetUI.cpp:1198) BEFORE the grid panes (1205). So when the Views editor commits a new column order mid-frame, the grid's post-block in the same frame compares the STALE old order against the freshly saved new order and reverts it.
scenario: Desktop, grid pane visible and focused (single-pane default). In the Views editor's Columns tab, drag 'Status' above 'Summary' and click Apply & Sync (or Ctrl+Enter / 'Save & switch'). viewsApplyAndSync -> ViewState.UpdateActive writes [id, status, summary] and enqueues the save. Later in the same frame drawActiveProjectGridPost runs with columns[] still [id, summary, status] (identity display order, no drag in progress): visualOrder [id, summary, status] != currentOrder [id, status, summary] -> ReorderViewColumns reverts the view, BumpRevision, and the 400ms autosave persists the old order. Next frame RebaseViewDraft adopts the reverted order into the editor draft, so the user's explicit Apply is silently undone (toast still says 'View saved'). Same for a newly checked field moved to a middle position (it lands back at the end). CLI view.* commands are unaffected only because MainThreadDispatcher::Drain runs before the frame-start cache build.

fix: Clamp at the command: reject or reset any non-finite width or one above a sane cap (e.g. !std::isfinite(width) || width > 10000 -> ValidationError or reset to 0) in RegisterViewSetColumnWidthCommand. Harden the load: read width only when colJson["width"].is_number() and the value is finite and in range, otherwise 0.0f (default). Optionally make NormalizeViewDefinition treat a non-finite width as unset so it can never reach disk.
problem: The v3 load path reads each column width with colJson.value("width", 0.0f) with no is_number()/finite check (the legacy branch at line 78 does check is_number). A non-number width (null or string) throws nlohmann type_error.302 out of ParseViewDefinition -> ParseWorkspaceObject; LoadPersistentViewsFromDisk's catch returns a PARTIAL file missing that backend and every alphabetically-later one, and Views::ApplyTrackerFromConfig then bootstraps a default bucket and enqueues a whole-file rewrite (WritePersistentViews), permanently dropping the user's saved views. The app itself can write such a width: view.set_column_width (ViewCommands.cpp:485/494) accepts any number — CommandRegistry coerces the string 'inf' via std::stod to +inf, and `width > 0.0f` stores it; NormalizeViewDefinition keeps it (inf > 0); nlohmann serializes the non-finite float as null.
scenario: `Smatchet.exe cmd view.set_column_width --key=field:summary --width=inf` (or 1e39 via CLI/MCP/Lua) on a Jira view -> Views::Update saves `"width": null` into smatchet_views.json (the live grid also gets WidthRequest=inf). On the next launch ParseViewDefinition throws on the null width; the Jira, Linear and Plane buckets are dropped from the loaded file, Jira is re-bootstrapped with defaults, and the enqueued rewrite overwrites the file — all saved views for those backends are lost. A hand-edited `"width": "200"` has the same effect.

fix: In NormalizeViewDefinition, drop any canonical key that is not "id" and not "field:" followed by a non-empty id. In ParseColumnKeysArg/view.create/view.update, either map a bare id to "field:<id>" or return the rejected keys in an `ignored` array, as view.set_column_order does. Independently, the CaptureHeaderDragColumnOrder guard from the stale-columns finding (only commit when visualOrder differs from the rendered columns[] order) stops the per-frame loop.
problem: NormalizeViewDefinition only drops empty and duplicate keys. Any other key that is neither "id" nor "field:<id>" is kept in Columns, but TicketGridColumnsBuilder::Build skips it (TicketGridModel.cpp:201-203) and FieldIdsFromColumns ignores it. view.create/view.update `columns` (ParseColumnKeysArg, ViewCommands.cpp:55-65) accept such keys silently, and the v3 load path accepts them too. As a result the rendered key sequence can never equal activeView.Columns. CaptureHeaderDragColumnOrder (SmatchetActiveProjectGridTable.cpp:502-512) therefore runs ReorderViewColumns, then BumpRevision, and re-arms viewLayoutSaveAt on EVERY frame.
scenario: `Smatchet.exe cmd view.update --columns='["summary","status"]'` (bare field ids, the shape the sibling `fields` param takes) returns success. The view becomes [id, summary, status] with Fields=[], so the grid shows only ID. From then on, while that pane is focused, every frame bumps the views revision. That rebuilds the TrackerFieldCatalogIndex and the grid columns each frame (SmatchetUI.cpp:836-843). The 400ms layout autosave is pushed out every frame and never fires, so later width and sort edits are not persisted. The bogus keys also cannot be removed from the UI: ApplyFieldSelectionToDraftColumns keeps non-'field:' keys, and the Columns tab only reorders.

fix: On shutdown (before the config-save worker is flushed and joined in ~AppController), drain a pending viewLayoutSaveAt != max. While viewsDirty is set, persist layout WITHOUT the unconfirmed query instead of deferring. For example, serialize the active view with Jql replaced by viewsOriginalSnapshot.Jql through a Views save variant, so layout is never held hostage by the query strip.
problem: The debounced layout autosave introduced here has no teardown flush, and while viewsDirty is set it is deferred indefinitely (re-armed +400ms every drain). viewLayoutSaveAt is only drained in drawEndOfFramePersistence. Nothing in ShutdownApplication / SmatchetUI / Views teardown persists a pending layout edit (Views has no destructor; no other reader of viewLayoutSaveAt exists). Width/order/sort/hide-parents/story-group edits that the product now promises to autosave are lost on exit.
scenario: (a) The user applies a JQL query in the grid search box. applyQueryToPaneView sets viewsDirty and the strip appears, which the user ignores. The user then resizes and drag-reorders columns and sorts, and the drain keeps deferring. The user quits without Save/Discard, and all those layout edits are lost on the next launch. (b) A resize/sort made within 400ms of closing the window is also dropped.

fix: Call NormalizeViewDefinition(updated) before building the dry-run output; it is idempotent with the normalize Views::Update already runs.
problem: view.update's dry-run reports updated.Columns un-normalized, but the real run normalizes inside Views::Update. The preview can omit the auto-added "id", show width 0 instead of the 90/180 defaults, and miss canonicalization, dedup and the SortSpecs pruning.
scenario: `view.update --columns='["field:summary"]' --dry-run` previews [{key:field:summary,width:0}], while the real call stores [{key:id,width:90},{key:field:summary,width:180}]. A script that trusts wouldDo is misled.

fix: Move the paragraph below the table (after line 210), or move the two view.toggle.* rows above it.
problem: The new `columns` explanatory paragraph (lines 205-208) was inserted in the middle of the `view` command table, before the `view.toggle.<id>` and `view.toggle.notifications` rows. In GFM the table ends at the blank line, and lines 209-210 (no blank line after the paragraph) become lazy-continuation text of that paragraph.
scenario: Rendered docs show the two view.toggle.* commands as raw pipe-delimited text appended to the `columns` paragraph instead of as table rows.

fix: Wrap the call the same way UpdateTicketInContext_ does: try { Cache->SaveTickets(backendKey, updatedTickets); } catch (const std::exception& ex) { LOG_ERROR("AppController::applyChangeProbeOnMainThread_ cache write failed pane='%s' key='%s' rows=%zu err=%s", paneId.c_str(), backendKey.c_str(), updatedTickets.size(), ex.what()); }. The in-memory merge has already been published, so the function should continue to the Lua notify, the toasts and the anchor advance. A stale cache row converges on the next sync.
problem: Cache->SaveTickets(backendKey, updatedTickets) runs bare inside applyChangeProbeOnMainThread_, which is a MainThreadDispatcher post-back (posted at line 648). LocalCacheManager::SaveTickets -> RunWriteTxnWithBusyRetry rethrows SQLite::Exception once the 500 ms BUSY budget is spent, and immediately for non-BUSY errors (SQLITE_FULL, IOERR, READONLY). MainThreadDispatcher::Drain (MainThreadDispatcher.h:86-88) invokes tasks with no try/catch, and the frame-loop call (Ui/SmatchetUI.cpp:822) is not guarded either, so the exception unwinds to main's entry-point catch (Standalone/main.cpp:1106) -> ShutdownApplication + exit code 1. UpdateTicketInContext_ (AppController_CatalogAndFieldEdit.cpp:152-170) documents exactly this hazard and wraps its SaveTicket in try/catch; this path does not.
scenario: The change monitor polls in the background with no user action. A remote edit lands on a ticket the pane shows, so updatedTickets is non-empty. The SQLite write then fails: a second Smatchet instance holds a write transaction on the shared cache past the retry budget, the disk is full, or AV/OneDrive locking on Windows returns IOERR. SaveTickets throws, the exception escapes Drain, and the app exits (Pillar 3 'never crash'). The rest of the frame's queued tasks are dropped as well.

fix: Inside the merge loop, under the lock, carry the lazy fields forward before comparing: CachedTicket incoming = t; smatchet::sync::LazyCommentFields lazy; if (smatchet::sync::SnapshotLazyCommentFields(*it, lazy)) { smatchet::sync::CarryForwardLazyCommentFields(lazy, incoming); }. Then compare and assign incoming in place of t, and push incoming into updatedTickets. Include "Sync/LazyEnrichmentCarryForwardPure.h". Add a doctest covering: a resident row with thread and blob, plus a fetched row with the same count and changed status, keeps the thread and blob after the merge.
problem: The change-probe merge replaces the resident row wholesale (*it = t; updatedTickets.push_back(t)) and persists it at line 793 without the lazy-comment carry-forward. Both sync apply paths run that carry-forward before replacing rows (TicketSyncService.cpp:186 ApplyIssueFetchPack and :436 DrainPendingStreamingBatches, via CarryForwardLazyComments / LazyEnrichmentCarryForwardPure.h, added later in #2255 for Pillar 6). GitHub list rows, and Jira rows whose follow-up comment fetch failed, carry no fieldValues["comment"] blob and no fieldRichValues["comment_thread"]. If the resident row holds a lazily fetched thread, the fieldValues/fieldRichValues comparison at line 775 is true even when only the lazy fields differ. The overwrite then drops the thread and the tooltip blob from memory, and writeTicketRows_ deletes them from tickets_v2. The comment at line 755 says this path mirrors DrainPendingStreamingBatches, but it no longer does.
scenario: On a GitHub pane the user posts a comment from the comments modal. The post-success re-fetch stores comments=N+1, the blob and comment_thread on the row (UpdateCachedCommentsFromThread -> UpdateTicket -> SaveTicket). GitHub bumps the issue's updated timestamp, so the next change poll (updated:>= window) returns the issue with comments=N+1 but no blob or thread. Line 775 sees a difference, line 776 overwrites the row, and line 793 persists the stripped row. When the user goes offline later, the comments modal has no cached thread to show (SeedThread is empty) and the Comments-cell tooltip has lost its blob. Online, each poll that catches a remote edit to such a ticket wipes the thread and forces a redundant lazy re-fetch.

fix: In the `status_code != 200` branch, build the detail with DescribeRejectedHttpStatus("Fetch issue transitions", response.status_code, response.error.message) and return Err(ClassifyRejectedHttpStatus(response.status_code, detail)) instead of TrackerErrorFromHttpStatus. That maps 2xx-non-200 to Unknown with the detail kept and status 0 to Transport, matching FetchFieldCatalog and FetchProjectComponents.
problem: JiraClient::FetchIssueTransitions enters its failure branch on `response.status_code != 200` and then classifies with TrackerErrorFromHttpStatus, which maps any 2xx to TrackerError::Ok() (Kind None, detail dropped). A 2xx other than 200 therefore returns Result::Err carrying an Ok-kind error, so the failure loses its kind and its detail. The sibling FetchProjectComponents in the same file (lines 520-525) guards this case explicitly, and Tracker/AGENTS.md names ClassifyRejectedHttpStatus as the helper for failure branches. On status 0 the detail also leaves out the transport message that DescribeRejectedHttpStatus would add.
scenario: A proxy or gateway answers GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/transitions with 203 or 204. FetchIssueTransitions returns Err(kind=None, detail=""). IssueTransitionsCacheService logs 'transitions fetch failed ... kind=ok', and KeyedLookupCache::CompleteFailure records LastErrorKind=None with an empty LastError. The backoff and the freshness cue still work because LastAttemptFailed is set, so the impact is limited to diagnostics: the failure is misreported as kind 'ok' and the HTTP detail is lost. Today this is dormant, because Jira answers this endpoint with 200.

fix: Move the end-of-frame restore out of SmatchetUI::Draw into a new SmatchetUI::EndFrame(UiDrawSession&), or an equivalent public hook. It should call drawMobileRestoreDesktopIni(d) when effectiveUiMode == Desktop and mobileDockSeeded is set. Have every host call it after pluginHost.OnDraw / Plugins.OnDraw and immediately before ImGui::Render(): Source/Standalone/main.cpp and StandaloneAppBootstrap.cpp (SmatchetDrawFrame), Source/Mobile/Android/android_main.cpp after s.pluginHost->OnDraw, and Source/Core/src/Ui/SmatchetImGuiHost.cpp after ImplData->Plugins.OnDraw. Then fix the two comments. Extend mobile_desktop_layout_roundtrip.test.cpp so the pre-flip snapshot includes a plugin-submitted docked window, for example a registered Lua window or the Scripting window opened, and assert it keeps its dock id.
problem: The Mobile->Desktop ini restore runs at the end of SmatchetUI::Draw, but that is not the end of the ImGui frame. Every host calls the plugin host after Draw and before ImGui::Render(): Standalone main.cpp:165-166 and StandaloneAppBootstrap.cpp:165-166 (mainWindow.Draw then pluginHost.OnDraw), android_main.cpp:656-657, and SmatchetImGuiHost.cpp:717-718. LuaConsolePlugin::OnDraw submits the 'Scripting' window, and AppController::DrawLuaWindows (AppController_LuaBindings_Draw.cpp:1228) submits every user Lua window with a plain, dockable ImGui::Begin. Those windows are submitted after drawMobileRestoreDesktopIni has already run ClearIniSettings and LoadIniSettingsFromDisk. ApplyWindowSettings plus DockContextBuildAddWindowsToNodes rebind them to the rebuilt desktop nodes. Those nodes have LastFrameAlive == -1, because only DockNodeUpdate sets it (imgui.cpp:19009) and the host's DockSpaceOverViewport already walked the old tree this frame. So BeginDocked undocks them (imgui.cpp:21208) with clear_persistent_docking_ref=true and calls MarkIniSettingsDirty(). This is the same undock the PR fixed for SmatchetUI's own windows. The comments at SmatchetMobileShellUi.cpp:503-505 and SmatchetUI.cpp:385-390 claim the restore runs 'after every window has ended', which is false for plugin windows.
scenario: Lua automation is on (default ON). A user script registers a window and the user docks it, for example as a tab in the bottom panel. In Auto UI mode the user narrows the app window past the mobile breakpoint, then widens it back. On the edge frame SmatchetUI::Draw restores the desktop ini, then PluginHost::OnDraw -> DrawLuaWindows -> Begin(name) undocks the script window (DockId cleared). It comes back floating, and ImGui's autosave writes the floating layout to imgui.ini, so the docking is permanently lost on every round-trip. The 'Scripting' window, when open, also undocks on that frame; RepairLuaWindowLayout then force-re-docks it into kBottomPanel, so it flashes floating and lands in the default slot. The bucket-E test does not catch this because cfg.ShowLuaAutomationWindow defaults to false and the test host has no Lua script windows.

fix: After the frame loop, assert the round-trip completed: IM_CHECK_NO_RET(!g_ui.mobileDockSeeded), IM_CHECK_NO_RET(::ImGui::GetIO().IniFilename != nullptr), and at least IM_CHECK_NO_RET(remaining < docked.size()). Better still, IM_CHECK_NO_RET(remaining == 0), since every snapshotted window was active the frame before the flip and should re-submit within one or two frames of the return.
problem: The regression guard passes with zero docking assertions when no pre-flip docked window is re-submitted within the 120-frame budget. `remaining > 0` only logs an info 'note', and nothing asserts that the round-trip actually returned to the desktop path (mobileDockSeeded cleared, io.IniFilename re-attached). If remaining == docked.size(), the IM_CHECK at line 132 never runs and the test reports PASS.
scenario: A future regression leaves mobileDockSeeded latched, for example drawMobileRestoreDesktopIni early-returning or the end-of-frame call being dropped from SmatchetUI.cpp:395-397. SmatchetUI::Draw then stays in the mobile fork forever after the mode returns to Desktop, and no desktop window is ever re-submitted. fix: Size the button from its label instead of a pixel literal: width = ImGui::CalcTextSize(SmatchetIconLeadingLabel(SmatchetAreFaIconsLoaded(), ICON_FA_ARROWS_ROTATE, SmatchetLocalization::TranslateSource("Save & Sync")).c_str()).x + 2 * style.FramePadding.x. problem: In combo mode the Save & Sync button has a hard-coded width of 140 px (ImVec2(140.0f, 0.0f)), and the combo reserves the same literal (line 209). The width is not scaled for DPI or font size. ImGui::Button with an explicit width clips its label to the frame. Combo mode is the only presentation on mobile: ResolvePrefsNavUseCombo returns true whenever embedded/mobileUi is set, and SmatchetMobileShellUi.cpp:248 calls drawPreferencesWindow(app, d, /*embedded=*/true). The commit says it fixes button clipping in this mode, but it does not. The comment on line 208 also gives the item spacing as 4 px. ApplyCommonStyle sets ItemSpacing.x to 8, and ScaleAllSizes scales it further.
scenario: On Android, android_main.cpp scales the font atlas by the host density (about 2.6x on a typical phone), and drawApplyAppearanceSettings multiplies FontGlobalScale by the touch density. That puts the font at about 40 px or more, so the label '<arrows-rotate glyph> Save & Sync' needs roughly 300 px plus the scaled FramePadding. The button is still 140 px, so only about the first half of the label shows (for example '(glyph) Save'). This happens on every HiDPI phone. Narrow desktop windows below 30 em hit the same clipping once FontSizePt is about 22 or larger (FontGlobalScale of about 1.4 or more).

fix: Restore the explicit split: 'float paneHeight = bodyHeight; if (d.prefsNavCombo) { paneHeight = ImGui::GetContentRegionAvail().y; } else { ImGui::SameLine(); }'. Update the comment so the combo branch's re-measure is the only measurement.

GetContentRegionAvail().y therefore returns -ItemSpacing.y, not the rail height. scenario: On desktop in rail mode (width above 32.5 em), BeginChild("PrefsBody", ImVec2(0, -ItemSpacing.y)) runs after SameLine. The right pane comes out ItemSpacing.y shorter than the nav rail: 6 px at Normal density, more when ScaleAllSizes applies. Its scroll region also ends early. The effect is cosmetic, and the layout now depends on a negative-size side effect instead of an explicit height.

fix: In DiscardQueuedGridFieldEditsOnBackendSwitch, keep queued edits whose Target.PaneId is non-empty, because they are already bound to their pane's backend, BackendKey and generation. Discard only unbound edits (Target.PaneId empty): PumpGridFieldEdits would bind those to the newly focused pane. Alternatively, bind them to the previously focused pane's target before the switch. Set the error banner only when something was actually discarded. Update the SmatchetGridUiSupport.h:93-95 doc comment and the SmatchetUI.cpp:738-739 comment to match. The later ResetOnCacheSiteChange call at SmatchetUI.cpp:712 (#2273) needs the same change. Add a doctest: queue a pane-bound edit, call the discard helper, and assert the edit survives while an unbound one is dropped.
problem: The session-level backend-change reset calls DiscardQueuedGridFieldEditsOnBackendSwitch (Source/Core/src/SmatchetGridFieldEditPipeline.cpp:229-237), which drops every queued grid edit. This reset also fires on every cross-backend pane-focus hop: Source/Core/src/Ui/SmatchetGridPaneWindows.cpp:291 sets d.cfg.TrackerType = pane.backendKey. Since #2260/S10, each queued PendingFieldEdit carries its own PendingActionTarget (PaneId, Backend, BackendKey, BackendGeneration), set at SmatchetActiveProjectGridUi.cpp:293-296. The worker sends through target.Backend (FieldEditPipelineService::SubmitFieldEditNetworkOnly, FieldEditPipelineService.cpp:219-223), and the local apply is generation-gated. So these edits would have reached the right tracker, and discarding them loses the user's writes for no reason. The header doc at Source/Core/include/Ui/SmatchetGridUiSupport.h:93-95 says the edits 'name the previous backend's issues, so they must never reach the new backend'. That has been stale since #2260.
scenario: Two grid panes: pane A on Jira, pane B on Linear. In pane A the user edits cell 1, which is dispatched and in flight, then edits cell 2, which is queued behind it, then clicks pane B before the first commit returns. A second case uses this PR's own hold path (SmatchetGridFieldEditPipeline.cpp:209): pane A shows a tracker error banner, so the grid is read-only and queued edits are held, and the user then clicks pane B. On the next frame drawViewStateAndConnectivity sees lastViewsBackendKey 'Jira' != 'Linear' and runs DiscardQueuedGridFieldEditsOnBackendSwitch. Cell 2's edit is cleared from d.queuedFieldEdits with 'Unsent edits discarded: the tracker backend changed...'. It is never sent and never written to the offline queue, so the user's edit is lost. The banner does not say which edits were dropped.

fix: Copy the field as soon as it is looked up and use the copy afterwards. For example, `const TrackerField* found = app->FindFieldById("status"); ... if (!found) return; const TrackerField statusField = *found;`, then `edit.Field = statusField;`. Never keep a FindFieldById pointer across ctx->Yield().
problem: StatusEdit_OfflineQueuesThenReplays takes a raw `const TrackerField*` from AppController::FindFieldById (line 253) and keeps it while it waits through ImGui frames (WaitForConnectivity at 270 and 272). It dereferences that pointer at line 279 (`edit.Field = *statusField`). FindFieldById returns a pointer into the focused catalog's `AvailableFields` vector and only holds `availableFieldsMutex_` during the lookup. On any frame where a field-catalog fetch future completes, the UI thread runs SetFieldCatalog, which does `cat.AvailableFields = std::move(fields)` (AppController_CatalogAndFieldEdit.cpp:505) and then push_backs into it (EnsureCatalogHistoryField / EnsureCatalogCommentsField). Either one frees the buffer the test still points at.
scenario: The previous test, StatusCombo_OfflineShowsOptions, ends by restoring the network and waiting for AuthenticatedReachable (line 230). Consuming that recovery sets g_ui.triggerCatalogRefetch (SmatchetUI.cpp:805), so an async catalog fetch starts against the fake backend. If that future completes during this test's WaitForConnectivity(TransportDown) frames, which come after line 253 but before line 279, then SetFieldCatalog swaps the vector and `*statusField` reads freed memory. The result is a heap use-after-free: an ASan report or crash in the bucket-E UI test binary, or a garbage TrackerField copied into the edit and a flaky failure.

fix: Surface the queued state on the result. For example, add `bool NeedsReview` (or the stored state string) to PendingActionSubmitResult and set it in PendingActionQueueService::SubmitOrQueue when a WorklogAdd is enqueued as kAmbiguous. Simpler still, enqueue that row directly as kNeedsReview, since replay would only move it there. In ApplyWorklogSaveResult, show a distinct warning toast for it, e.g. 'The tracker did not answer, so the worklog may already be logged. Check <issue>, then send or discard it in the Offline Queue panel.' Add a localization key for that text, and add "needsReview": true to PendingActionSuccessData. Cover it with a PendingActionQueueService case asserting the flag on the ambiguous-worklog submit.
problem: A worklog whose live send failed AFTER the request went out (timeout / 5xx: StateAfterFailedSend -> kAmbiguous) comes back as Kind::Queued, and ApplyWorklogSaveResult shows the generic 'Worklog queued offline - Saved offline; it will be logged when the tracker is reachable.' toast (SmatchetLocalization.cpp:875-877) and closes the dialog. But replay never sends an ambiguous worklog: PendingActionQueueService::ReplayOne moves it to needs_review ('Sent, but the response was lost...') and IsReplayable skips it, so nothing is logged automatically, and the worklog may in fact already be on the tracker. PendingActionSubmitResult carries no queued state, so the UI cannot tell the two cases apart. The ticket.add_worklog envelope (BuiltinCommands_TicketMutations.cpp:142, PendingActionSuccessData) reports the same plain "queued": true. This contradicts Pillar 6 rule 'toasts say what actually happened' and the ADR-0026 text (line 36: 'a worklog in that state waits for the user's review').
scenario: Online, the user saves a 2h worklog; Jira accepts the POST but the response times out (TrackerErrorTransport after the send). SubmitOrQueue enqueues it as 'ambiguous' and returns Queued. The dialog closes with 'Saved offline; it will be logged when the tracker is reachable.' On the next replay pass the row becomes needs_review and stays there. The user trusts the toast and never opens the Offline Queue panel. Either the worklog already landed (and the user may log it again by hand, thinking it is still pending), or it did not land and is never logged. An MCP/CLI caller of ticket.add_worklog sees the same 'queued' and assumes it will be sent.

fix: At replay, rebuild the untouched estimate from the server's current value before sending. EvaluateFieldEditConflict already fetches `fresh` for a based row. When the payload is a sole `timetracking` object, set the non-edited key (remainingEstimate for timeoriginalestimate, and vice versa) to fresh.GetFieldValue(<other field id>), or drop it when the server value is empty. Do the same in ResolveFieldEditConflict/RebuildSpecialQueuedPayload, or re-derive it at replay so a resolved row picks it up too. An alternative is to capture a base for both estimates at enqueue time and suspend as a conflict when either one moved. Add an OfflineQueueServiceRuntime case: queue an originalEstimate edit, change the fake server's remaining estimate, replay, and assert the PUT carries the server's remaining estimate, not the snapshot.
problem: PR #2262 made Jira estimate edits queueable offline. The queued payload is the full `timetracking` object (TrackerFieldPayloadPure::BuildTimetrackingEstimateEdit, TrackerFieldPayloadPure.cpp:772-788, queued by FieldEditPipelineService::TryPrepareOfflineFieldEdit at FieldEditPipelineService.cpp:368-375). It holds the edited estimate plus the OTHER estimate, copied from the pane's cached ticket at enqueue time (req.Original/RemainingEstimateSnapshot). Replay (ReplayOneFieldEdit, lines 1200-1204) PUTs that payload unchanged. The conflict check before it (EvaluateFieldEditConflict -> ResolveFieldEditScalarConflict) compares only the edited estimate (row.FieldId) against the fresh server ticket, so a server-side change to the untouched estimate during the offline window is silently overwritten with the stale snapshot. Conflict resolution has the same gap: RebuildSpecialQueuedPayload (TrackerFieldPayloadPure.cpp:863-866) replaces only the edited key and keeps the stale other estimate, even when the user picks 'Use Theirs'.
scenario: A user goes offline and edits Original Estimate on PROJ-1 from 2h to 3h in the grid. The queued row is {"timetracking":{"originalEstimate":"3h","remainingEstimate":"2h"}}, with the remaining estimate taken from the snapshot. Meanwhile a teammate logs 1h of work, and Jira auto-adjusts Remaining Estimate to 1h. On reconnect the replay re-fetches PROJ-1: timeoriginalestimate is still 2h, which equals the captured base, so the conflict check returns Proceed. The PUT then sets remainingEstimate back to 2h. The teammate's adjustment is lost on a field this user never edited, with no conflict prompt. If the edited estimate itself conflicted and the user chooses 'Use Theirs', the re-queued payload still writes the stale remaining estimate.

fix: In ResetOnCacheSiteChange, do not touch fieldCatalogLoading or fieldCatalogFuture: set only triggerCatalogRefetch = true and clear fieldCatalogWarning. The result guard at SmatchetUI.cpp:1515-1521 already discards a finished fetch whose CacheBackendKey differs from FocusedCacheBackendKey() and re-triggers the fetch, so the stale in-flight result is dropped without blocking. Alternatively, hand the old future to a background drain before restarting. Apply the same change to the kind-switch reset at lines 745-746.
problem: ResetOnCacheSiteChange sets d.fieldCatalogLoading = false while d.fieldCatalogFuture may still hold an in-flight std::async(std::launch::async) catalog fetch. In the same frame, drawEnsureCatalogAndInitialSync (SmatchetUI.cpp:1506-1508) sees !fieldCatalogLoading plus triggerCatalogRefetch and runs `d.fieldCatalogFuture = StartFieldCatalogFetchAsync(...)` (SmatchetUI.cpp:1503). Move-assigning over a running std::async future releases its shared state, and that release joins the async thread on both MSVC and libstdc++. The UI thread then blocks until the old network fetch returns. This is a Pillar 2 freeze with no visible cue. The kind-switch reset at lines 745-746 has the same pattern.
scenario: The user picks another Jira site in the Views domain combo (SmatchetViewsDashboardUi.cpp:1142-1148) while a ticket sync is running. SyncWithBackend defers the request (TicketSyncService.cpp:691-699), so the key does not change yet. The combo's triggerCatalogRefetch starts a catalog fetch on the next frame. When the deferred sync starts, SwapBackendIfTrackerChanged re-stamps the site key and ResetOnCacheSiteChange fires on the following frame. It clears fieldCatalogLoading, and the next start blocks the frame for the rest of the first fetch: seconds on Jira Cloud, or up to the HTTP timeout on a slow link. The same freeze happens when a post-sync catalog refetch (ConsumeFieldCatalogRefetchAfterLiveTicketSync) is still in flight as the user switches site or account.

fix: Clear the in-memory catalog through a path that does not persist. For example, add AppController::ClearFieldCatalogInMemory(): under availableFieldsMutex_ it resets AvailableFields, AvailableComponents and AvailableIssueTypeMeta, sets fieldCatalogEverLoaded_ = false, clears the catalog error and warning, and bumps TrackerFieldCatalogRevision, without calling SaveFieldCatalogSnapshot. Call it here and at the twin call sites (SmatchetUI.cpp:741, SmatchetPreferencesUi.cpp:1202). Or have SetFieldCatalog skip the snapshot save when error is empty and all three arrays are empty.
problem: On a site switch, `app.SetFieldCatalog({}, {}, {}, std::string())` is meant to clear the catalog in memory, but SetFieldCatalog (AppController_CatalogAndFieldEdit.cpp:416-467) also persists it. It builds catalogCacheKey from ConfigManager::Load() and cat.currentCatalogProjectKey_, then calls FieldCatalogCache::SaveFieldCatalogSnapshot with the empty arrays. That overwrites the on-disk offline catalog snapshot of a site with an empty entry. TryLoadFieldCatalogSnapshot (FieldCatalogCache.cpp:456-499) later restores the empty entry as a valid snapshot. This breaks the Pillar 6 rule that cached data is never wiped. It also adds a synchronous read, parse and write of the catalog cache file, plus a possible config disk re-read, to the UI thread.
scenario: Jira sites A and B have both been used, so the snapshots 'Jira|A|PROJ' and 'Jira|B|PROJ' exist. The user is offline and switches to B in the Views domain combo, which calls ConfigManager::Save first, so Load() now returns B. On the next frame, ResetOnCacheSiteChange writes an empty entry to 'Jira|B|PROJ'; currentCatalogProjectKey_ is still PROJ. B's catalog fetch then fails offline. SmatchetUI.cpp:1541 calls SetFieldCatalog({}, {}, error), and HandleFieldCatalogError -> TryLoadFieldCatalogSnapshot('Jira|B|PROJ') loads the empty entry. The grid shows 'restored ... field catalog from local snapshot' with no fields, components or issue-type metadata. B's real snapshot is lost until an online fetch succeeds. After a debounced Preferences change, Load() can still return A, and the wipe hits A's snapshot instead.

fix: Count only in UI-test builds (#if defined(SMATCHET_BUILD_UI_TESTS) around the increment), or make the counter unsigned and saturating (if (s_heldRowsDrawn < INT_MAX) ++s_heldRowsDrawn;).
problem: The test hook counter s_heldRowsDrawn (line 44) is a signed int. Production code increments it on every frame for every held row drawn, in both offline-queue tables (SmatchetOfflineQueueUi.cpp:997 and SmatchetOfflineQueueUi_Actions.cpp:180). Only ResetHeldRowsDrawnForTests ever resets it, and only bucket-E tests call that. The counter grows for as long as the app runs and eventually hits signed overflow, which is undefined behaviour (Pillar 3: no silent UB).
scenario: A user keeps queued writes for a site no open pane uses, for example after changing the Jira account, and leaves the Offline Queue panel visible. With 20 held rows at 144 fps the counter grows by about 2,880 per second and passes INT_MAX after about 8.6 days of uptime. UBSan reports the overflow, and the compiler may assume it never happens.

fix: Accumulate wheel delta in SmatchetUI::dispatchKeybindings instead of firing on the sign. Add a float member wheelZoomAccum_. On frames where a wheel binding's modifiers match, add io.MouseWheel to it, and reset it when the sign flips or the modifier match drops. Fire a wheel binding only when the accumulator reaches +/-1.0 (one notch = WHEEL_DELTA), then subtract 1.0. Still clear io.MouseWheel every frame a wheel binding matched, so scrolling is suppressed even below the threshold. Keep MatchHotkey's sign test for capture. Also take persistence off the per-step path: in AdjustFontSize, replace the direct ConfigManager::Save(g_ui.cfg) with the coalescing off-thread smatchet::config_save::EnqueueTrackerConfig(g_ui.cfg), the same path SmatchetAiAssistantUi uses. Add a bucket-E test: inject 10 Ctrl+wheel events of 0.1 each and assert FontSizePt rises by exactly 1.
problem: Wheel bindings fire on the bare sign of io.MouseWheel with no delta accumulation (MatchHotkey wheel branch ImGuiHotkey.cpp:317-321, consumed in dispatchKeybindings SmatchetUI.cpp:1028-1034, defaulted onto ui.zoom.in/out at KeybindingsConfig.cpp:298-299). Any frame with a fractional, non-zero wheel delta counts as one full zoom step. Each step runs AdjustFontSize (BuiltinCommands_Ui.cpp:42), which calls ConfigManager::Save synchronously on the UI thread: a disk re-read and merge (LoadMergedConfigJson), DPAPI secret encryption (SaveSecretsAndPurgeLegacy) and an atomic file write. Before this PR, zoom only fired on a non-repeating key press. The new wheel trigger can fire on every frame.
scenario: On a Windows laptop with a Precision Touchpad, the user pinches or holds Ctrl and does a two-finger scroll. Windows sends this as Ctrl+WM_MOUSEWHEEL with small deltas (for example 8/120), and the ImGui GLFW/Win32 backends pass it through unquantized via AddMouseWheelEvent(delta/120). io.MouseWheel is a small non-zero value on nearly every frame of the gesture, so a short gesture of about 0.2 s at 144 Hz fires about 16-30 ui.zoom.in steps. The font jumps from 16pt to the 32pt clamp in one gesture, and each step does a synchronous config save on the UI thread, so frames hitch for the whole gesture (Pillars 1 and 2). A free-spinning high-resolution wheel shows the same runaway. The opposite case also exists: a fast notched spin that lands 3.0 in one frame zooms only once.

problem: ResolveAmbiguousComment decides retry-vs-final from the dedupe READ's error kind (`err.IsRetryable() ? kAmbiguous : ""`). On Jira, the primary backend, JiraClient::FetchIssueComments (JiraIssueSearch.cpp:850-853) collapses EVERY page failure -- network status 0, 5xx, 429 -- into TrackerErrorUnknown(..., 0). Unknown is not IsRetryable() and not IsTransport(), so a transient failure of the check is treated as a final rejection: RecordFailure archives the queued comment as `replay_rejected`, and TransportDown is never set, so the pass keeps going. Verified: TrackerError.h:54-57 (IsRetryable = Transport/RateLimited/ServerError only); GitHub and Plane classify via ClassifyRejectedHttpStatus, Jira does not. On reconnect the replay pass runs the dedupe fetch; Jira answers 503/429, or the network blips (status 0) -> Unknown -> the comment moves to the failed list ('(failed - see Offline Queue)') and is never auto-posted, though the tracker never rejected it. fix: Minimal: make the cache's on-disk file name ASCII-only (map bytes >= 0x80 to '_' in StoredFileName, or in a cache-specific wrapper) so every narrow consumer resolves the same file; entry.json keeps the URL for the lookup. Alternative: on _WIN32, convert FilePath UTF-8 to wide and call ShellExecuteW (SmatchetAttachmentPreviewUi.cpp already has Utf8ToWideLocal), and read the preview header with ghc::filesystem::ifstream.
problem: The attachment cache writes its data file through ghc::filesystem (fs::ofstream(fs::path(temp)) + fs::rename). On Windows, ghc reads a std::string path as UTF-8 and creates the real Unicode name; the code comment at lines 42-43 says so. StoredFileName/SanitizeFileName keep non-ASCII bytes (a UTF-8 name such as 'résumé.pdf', or a macOS screenshot name with U+202F before 'AM'). The path that comes back (LocalAttachment.FilePath, from ResolveLocalAttachment) then goes to narrow-ANSI consumers: ShellExecuteA in OpenAttachmentInSystemViewer (AttachmentAppUpdateService.cpp:429) and the preview dimension parse's std::ifstream(path.c_str()) (SmatchetAttachmentPreviewUi.cpp:86). Both decode the bytes with the ANSI code page, so they look for a mojibake name that does not exist. Before this commit the uncached temp file was written with a narrow std::ofstream (also ANSI), so the open path agreed with ShellExecuteA. The cache is now the normal path, and every later open (online or offline) is served from it. No UTF-8 activeCodePage manifest or setlocale(.UTF8) exists in the tree.
scenario: Windows, default non-UTF-8 ANSI code page. A Jira attachment named 'Screenshot 2026-09-29 at 10.15.42<U+202F>AM.png' (or 'résumé.pdf') is opened with 'Open in system viewer'. The cache stores it under its real Unicode name. ShellExecuteA gets the UTF-8 bytes, returns SE_ERR_FNF, and the user sees 'The file downloaded but the system viewer failed to launch.' This repeats on every later open, because the cache hit returns the same path. The in-app preview's dimension parse fails the same way ('Failed to open downloaded attachment file.').

So a failure on page 2 or later leaves the pages fetched so far. That breaks AppController.h:805-806, which promises that "an empty or failed fetch never replaces a saved roster". (2) In-memory wipe: on a page-1 failure the roster is empty. The seed at :1498-1500 ("until (or unless) this fetch brings a live one") is undone when :1533 SetAvailableUsers(empty) replaces the roster the seed restored. problem: The press frame can paint rows. The origin row opens the gesture mid-frame (Begin, then Frame=frame), so rows drawn AFTER it in the same frame pass GestureLapsed (the Frame==frame guard) and compute DraggedOver from this frame's MousePosPrev->MousePos segment. That segment is pointer travel from BEFORE the button went down. ImGui applies a mouse-move event and a button-down event in the same frame (the trickle queue only defers a move that comes after a button change), so prev!=cur is reachable on the press frame.
scenario: The pointer moves upward from row k+1 into row k and the user clicks in the same frame (a moving click; at 60 Hz it takes about 240 px/s to cover the 4 px inter-row gap in one frame). Row k opens the run with !row_k. Row k+1 is drawn later in that frame, its band lies on the prev->cur segment, and if its value differs it is painted and reported Changed. The adjacent field the user had just set gets silently flipped in the Views draft. This breaks the 'paint follows motion / never does anything unasked' contract. Rows above the origin are drawn earlier in the frame and are never affected, so only upward clicks hit this.

fix: Raise the bar only when no popup is open, for example `if (!::ImGui::IsPopupOpen("", ImGuiPopupFlags_AnyPopupId | ImGuiPopupFlags_AnyPopupLevel)) ::ImGui::BringWindowToDisplayFront(::ImGui::GetCurrentWindow());`. problem: DrawStatusBarAutoHide calls ImGui::BringWindowToDisplayFront on the floating ##StatusBarAutoHide window every frame it is visible. Dear ImGui (pinned 1.92.x docking) puts popups, menus and modals on the same display layer as ordinary windows (GetWindowDisplayLayer only lifts Tooltip windows to layer 1), and brings a popup to the front only when it appears or gets focus (Begin want_focus -> FocusWindow). Then open a context menu, a View dropdown or a long combo whose bottom lands in the last ~barH px of the window. ImGui clamps popups to the full viewport rect, not the work rect. A modal that reaches the bottom edge gets the bar drawn on top of it and its dimmed background, and that strip ignores clicks because the modal blocks hover on non-modal windows.

fix: Latch the pending single-column auto-fit before the next BeginTable consumes it. Example: in drawActiveProjectGridPost (table still current, after layout), store table->AutoFitSingleColumn on the GridPane. On the next frame, pass that index to SyncGridTableColumnWidths and skip it, so post-capture writes the fitted width into the view; then clear the latch. Add a bucket-E case that double-clicks a header border and checks the view width changes.
problem: SyncGridTableColumnWidths skips a column only when it is LastResizedColumn or has AutoFitQueue != 0. ImGui 1.92 (pinned 329c5a6b) does single-column auto-fit a different way. TableSetColumnWidthAutoSingle sets only table->AutoFitSingleColumn (plus CannotSkipItemsQueue). The next BeginTable then applies TableSetColumnWidth(n, WidthAuto) inside TableBeginApplyRequests and resets AutoFitSingleColumn to -1. The double-click path also sets held=false, so ResizedColumn and LastResizedColumn stay -1. drawActiveProjectGridSetup calls the sync right after TableSetupColumn, so it overwrites the fitted WidthRequest with the view's stored width before TableUpdateLayout runs. WidthGiven never changes, and drawActiveProjectGridPost's ShouldCaptureColumnWidth never sees a difference to persist.
scenario: Focused grid pane that owns its view (widthsArePanesOwn). The user double-clicks a column header's right border, or right-clicks the header and picks 'Size column to fit'. Frame N: TableUpdateBorders calls TableSetColumnWidthAutoSingle. Frame N+1: BeginTable sets WidthRequest = WidthAuto. SyncGridTableColumnWidths then sees LastResizedColumn == -1, AutoFitQueue == 0 and want != WidthRequest, so it sets WidthRequest = want (the old view width). The column snaps back and auto-fit silently does nothing. Before this change TableSetupColumn applied its width only at init, so the fit stuck and the post-capture autosaved it. 'Size all columns to fit' still works because it uses AutoFitQueue.

fix: In the else branch, skip the node when `display` is empty (`if (!display.empty()) { ... push textNode ... }`), as AdfEmitText does. problem: The external-image fallback builds the link text as `alt.empty() ? src : alt` and pushes it directly, without the empty-text guard that AdfEmitText has (`if (text.empty()) return;`). When both src and alt are empty, MarkdownToAdf emits {"type":"text","text":"","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":""}}]}. ADF requires a text node's text to be non-empty, so Jira rejects the whole document.
scenario: A user types `![]()` (or `![![]()]()`) in a Jira description or comment. md4c parses it as an image with an empty destination (CommonMark allows an omitted destination), LeaveImageSpan returns src="" and alt="", and line 344 pushes a text node with empty text. On save, Jira returns HTTP 400 INVALID_INPUT for the whole document. The test file already records that Jira 400s on invalid ADF.
